title: Embedded Control Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE 

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO 

- Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

- Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT 

In this role, you will play a key part in developing the embedded control platform and will translate functional and control requirements into embedded hardware and software architectures, select appropriate microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA, or other controller technologies, and develop real-time software close to the hardware implementation. Your work will directly influence the performance, reliability, safety, and will require close collaboration with power electronics, integrated electronics, mechanical, thermal, and system engineers.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 

- Define embedded controller architectures for power electronic converters and select suitable microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA.

- Translate power electronics and control requirements into efficient, deterministic, and robust real-time software implementations.

- Develop, test, debug, and validate embedded software on target hardware, from individual software blocks through complete controller implementations and automated testing environments to validate the design.

- Explore new controller technologies, embedded architectures, and software implementation concepts to improve converter performance, flexibility, reliability, functionality, and maintainability.

WHO YOU ARE 

- You hold a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- You have a strong understanding of embedded architectures, and the practical considerations involved in selecting controllers for demanding real-time applications.

- You are an expert in embedded software development for real-time applications, preferably in power electronics, industrial automation, or similar applications, spanning FPGA programming, systems programming, hardware interfaces and communication protocols.

- You are experienced in monitoring and debugging software directly on target hardware

NICE TO HAVE 

- Experience with model-based development, hardware-in-the-loop testing, automated testing, or safety-critical software development is a plus.

INTERVIEW PROCESS 

- Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

- Technical Screening (30 min)

- Technical Panel (3x60 min)

We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. title: Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer
description:
About Electra 

Air travel is about to become something more: more direct, more accessible, and more connected to the places where people live, work and want to be. Every day in the U.S., people make 35 million trips of 50–500 miles, stuck in traffic or routed through crowded hubs. Chances are, you've been one of them. At Electra, we're changing that with the EL9, a nine-passenger, hybrid-electric aircraft that takes off and lands in just 150 feet. Our Ultra Short technology opens up thousands of new places to fly, beyond conventional runways, congested airports and long drives. We're backed by Lockheed Martin, Honeywell and Safran. Operators worldwide have signed intent-to-purchase agreements for the first 2,200 aircraft we produce, and we're moving toward first test flights in 2027. 

Getting a new kind of aircraft airborne takes more than ambition. It takes our kind of bold: people who think big while working in the real world. Who move ideas into action and collaborate without silos. Who put people first and make room at the table for everyone. Who challenge one another without diminishing one another. 

Sound like you? Then look beyond what you thought were your own limits, and help us take flight beyond runways. 

The Role 

As Electra's Senior Structural Assembly Manufacturing Engineer, you'll play a key role in developing and industrializing the structural assembly processes for the EL9 aircraft, working from early product development through prototype build, production implementation, and ramp-up.

You'll work closely with Product Engineering during aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and can be efficiently, repeatably, and reliably produced. You'll bring a hands-on manufacturing perspective to structural design decisions, evaluating assembly sequence, tolerance management, access, tooling, fastening and joining methods, inspection requirements, producibility, and production risk.

As the EL9 transitions from design into physical hardware, you'll help translate released engineering into executable manufacturing processes and support prototype and initial aircraft builds. You'll work closely with airframe manufacturing suppliers, providing on-site Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support as needed to ensure proper information flow, resolve technical and quality issues, support the incorporation of product changes and support supply chain on contract management.

This is an opportunity to influence both how the aircraft is designed and how it is ultimately built, while helping establish Electra's structural assembly manufacturing supply chain capability from the ground up.

What You'll Do 

- Partner with Product Engineering throughout aircraft development to ensure structural designs incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles and support efficient, repeatable, and scalable production.

- Review aircraft structural designs, assemblies, drawings, models, and engineering changes from a manufacturing perspective, providing recommendations related to producibility, assembly sequence, access, tolerance stack-up, fastening and joining methods, tooling, inspection, and production risk.

- Participate in design trade studies, concept reviews, and design reviews, representing Manufacturing Engineering and identifying manufacturing constraints and opportunities early in the development cycle.

- Provide Manufacturing Engineering oversight and liaison support at airframe and structural suppliers, working directly with supplier manufacturing teams to clarify design and manufacturing intent, resolve producibility and assembly issues, and maintain program execution.

- Work closely with the airframe supplier Tooling Engineering to define assembly tooling concepts, requirements, locating strategies, interfaces, and implementation plans.

- Review supplier manufacturing approaches, build plans, assembly processes, tooling concepts, and production readiness to ensure alignment with Electra's engineering requirements and program objectives.

- Support prototype fabrication, development aircraft assembly, first builds, and production implementation, providing hands-on Manufacturing Engineering support to resolve issues encountered during structural assembly.

- Coordinate technical resolution of manufacturing issues and nonconformances with Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders.

- Capture manufacturing lessons learned and supplier feedback from prototype and initial production builds and drive those learnings back into product design, manufacturing processes, tooling, and planning.

- Support structural assembly production ramp-up by identifying constraints, resolving manufacturing issues, improving assembly processes, and driving improvements in quality, cost, schedule, and production rate.

- Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Electra manufacturing engineering standards, methods, processes, and best practices.

What You Bring 

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Aeronautical, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering field.

- 8+ years of aerospace manufacturing engineering experience, with significant experience in aircraft structural assembly and industrialization.

- Strong hands-on knowledge of aircraft structural assembly processes, including metallic and/or composite airframe structures, drilling, fastening, joining, shimming, sealing, alignment, and major structural integration.

- Demonstrated experience applying Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles during aircraft product development.

- Experience reviewing engineering drawings, 3D models, GD&T, tolerances, and engineering changes from a manufacturing and assembly perspective.

- Experience developing manufacturing plans, assembly sequences, work instructions, tooling requirements, and manufacturing engineering documentation.

- Experience supporting prototype, development, or first-production aircraft builds.

- Experience working directly with aircraft structures suppliers or manufacturing partners and supporting production activities in a factory environment.

- Demonstrated ability to work effectively across Product Engineering, Stress, Quality, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, Tooling, and Production organizations.

- Strong problem-solving skills and ability to make sound engineering recommendations in a fast-moving aircraft development environment.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across internal teams and external suppliers.

- Ability and willingness to travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as required by program needs.

Bonus Points

- Experience with aircraft assembly tooling, jigs, fixtures, determinant assembly, or advanced assembly methodologies.

When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.

The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

description:

We're looking for a senior engineer who lives at the seam between software and the network — someone who's built customer-facing APIs where a POST doesn't end at a database row, it ends at a router being configured in a PoP. You're strong in async Python, comfortable in Go, and you can read an FRR or VyOS config as easily as an application stack trace. Telnyx sells networking as an API product: Private Networks, WireGuard interfaces, Virtual Cross Connects into AWS/Azure/GCP, anycast Global IP, and Public Internet Gateways. This role is the full stack of that. You design the API resource, write the orchestration code that turns a request into a network deployment, and own the BGP config it renders onto the fleet. You'll be part of a small, focused team where you own products from the developer-facing spec all the way down to the config on the box — and where the network layer isn't someone else's problem, it's the point.

What you'll own 

- The public API on api.telnyx.com — /networks , /virtual_cross_connects , /wireguard_interfaces , /wireguard_peers , /global_ips , /public_internet_gateways and their coverage/health/usage endpoints. Resource modeling, OpenAPI 3 specs (public and private), edge API-gateway routing, and backward compatibility for live customers.

- The orchestration control plane (Python 3.12, asyncio) — translating POST/DELETE into network deployments: resource allocation (IPAM, port/route-distinguisher/GRE-ID pools), Postgres-backed job queues ( SKIP LOCKED ), retries, rollback on partial failure, deploy/decommission runners, and long-running health-check and reconciliation daemons.

- Cloud interconnect integrations — Equinix Fabric and Equinix Metal APIs to land virtual cross connects into AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud regions.

- Envoy-based data planes — a Go xDS control plane on envoyproxy/go-control-plane, pushing CDS/RDS/EDS over ADS to edge and gateway Envoy fleets.

- Production — Prometheus/Telegraf metrics and alerting, Bugsnag, customer escalations that span app logic and the network, and billing sync (MRC) for network resources.

Tech stack (what you'll actually touch) 

- Languages: Python (asyncio: aiohttp, uvloop, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, aiopg), Go (Envoy control plane), Jinja2, Bash

- Data: PostgreSQL (schema design, migrations, advisory locking, as a job queue), RabbitMQ

- Network OS / routing: VyOS, FRR, Linux networking (VRFs, netfilter/NAT, netplan, GRE, WireGuard), BGP (VRFs, route reflectors, communities/labels, anycast), Unbound

- Automation: Ansible / ansible-runner, netmiko, asyncssh, NetBox-style IPAM (pynetbox, netaddr)

- Proxy / data plane: Envoy, xDS (ADS, go-control-plane)

- Vendor & cloud: Equinix Fabric, Equinix Metal, AWS / Azure / GCP interconnect regions

- Platform: Docker/OCI, GitHub Actions, HashiCorp Vault, OpenAPI 3 + Redocly, pytest (unit → e2e), mypy/ruff/black

- Architecture: clean/hexagonal (usecases, repository interfaces, adapters) — the service is structured, not a script pile

Who we're looking for 

- You've built and operated customer-facing REST APIs over real infrastructure — APIs where a POST ends in a router being configured, not just a row inserted — and you've lived with the async-job, rollback, and eventual-consistency problems that creates.

- Strong async Python in production, and comfortable writing and reviewing Go.

- Working routing knowledge: you can configure and debug BGP sessions, VRFs, GRE tunnels, NAT, and WireGuard, and read FRR or VyOS configs. Certification not required; hands-on ability is.

- Postgres beyond ORM basics — migrations on live systems, locking semantics, queue patterns.

- Fleet automation over SSH — Ansible at production scale, idempotent roles, safe rollout/rollback, drift detection.

- You've debugged incidents across layers in one sitting — tcpdump , wg show , vtysh , and application logs — ending in either a code fix or a config fix, and knowing which.

Bonus points for

title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Benelux
description:
About Telnyx 

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network , to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications. 

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team. 

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers. 

The Role 

We're building a local Enterprise Sales Pod in Amsterdam — one AE and one Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), working together to build a Telnyx enterprise business in your market. You'll embed directly with enterprise customers to architect and ship production systems on Telnyx's global network — voice, messaging, AI, and wireless.

This isn't about demoing products. It's about building real solutions that work at scale.

You'll work side-by-side with a dedicated Enterprise AE — not a demo resource, but a commercial partner who owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, and closes the deal. You own the technical side: discovery, architecture, POC, and production go-live. You win together. No throw-over-the-wall.

The Pod Model 

Enterprise AE — owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, gets in the room, owns commercial qualification and close, expands the account. 

Forward Deployed Engineer — owns technical discovery, designs the architecture, builds the POC when gated, gets the first workload live, removes blockers and finds the next workload.

We sell the workload, not the SKU. Customers buy a production outcome — an AI contact center, a SOC/NOC agent, global communications, connected mobility, or enterprise inference — that runs on Telnyx primitives (voice, messaging, numbers, wireless, Voice AI, inference, agents, connectivity). You lead with the outcome conversation, not a product menu.

What You'll Do 

• Embed with enterprise customers to understand their communications workflows, AI use cases, and integration challenges firsthand
• Build and deploy custom implementations: AI Voice Assistants, Telnyx APIs (Voice, Messaging, Fax, Wireless), WebRTC
• Run open-weight LLMs in customer environments — consume GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, and MiniMax through Telnyx Inference (OpenAI-compatible API; there's no model infrastructure for you to run), or deploy self-hosted stacks (Llama, Mistral, and region-specific models like Mistral Large, GPT-NL, or other EU sovereign models) behind your own serving engine when air-gapped or sovereign-cloud requirements demand it
• Deploy and operate LiteLLM as the model gateway in customer environments: a unified OpenAI-compatible interface across self-hosted open-weight models and hosted providers, with routing, load balancing, retries and fallbacks, rate limits, and per-team virtual keys
• Instrument and govern LLM usage through the gateway — cost tracking and budgets, caching, logging and observability (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, or similar), and guardrails — so customers can see and control what their AI workloads are doing
• Wire production observability for everything you ship — metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerting (e.g. Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, OpenTelemetry for traces, Graylog or ELK for logs — or the customer's existing stack) — so you and the customer's ops team both know what "healthy" looks like and what pages whom when it isn't
• Design model routing strategies for real-time voice workloads, balancing latency, cost, and quality, with sane fallback behavior when a provider degrades
• Make the build-vs-buy case between self-hosted open-weight models and hosted frontier APIs, and keep the customer's application code portable across both
• Adapt models to customer domains: prompt and RAG pipelines and evaluation harnesses for Dutch and French language use cases and Benelux/EU-specific regulatory environments (GDPR, EU AI Act, Dutch data protection, Belgian data protection)
• Lead POCs, pilots, and production launches from whiteboard to go-live
• Own customer outcomes — stay engaged until the solution is live and stable
• Collaborate directly with Product and Engineering to shape the roadmap based on field insights from the Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg

• Create clear technical documentation, runbooks, and maintainable solutions for handoff
• Troubleshoot and resolve complex integration issues alongside customer teams

What We're Looking For 

• CS degree or equivalent experience
• 3+ years building and shipping production software — you've written code that real users depended on, you've been on-call for it, and you've debugged it when things broke. (A consulting background counts if this is also true of you.)
• Proficiency in multiple languages: Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Go — you're more dangerous in some than others. (Telnyx Edge Compute — functions and stateful actors — is TypeScript, so that one pulls double duty.)
• Practical understanding of what breaks in front of a model in production: provider rate limits and quotas, timeout and retry behavior, streaming, token accounting and cost attribution, and the failure modes that only show up under concurrency
• Comfortable deploying containerized services on Kubernetes, with secrets management, config, and upgrades as part of the deployment story
• You've wired observability and been paged because of it — Prometheus + Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Graylog, ELK, or equivalent. You know what to monitor, what to alert on, and what "healthy" looks like
• High-concurrency experience — Kafka, message queues, or event streams at real scale. When throughput spikes you know what breaks — consumer lag, backpressure, hot partitions, rebalance stalls — and what absorbs it: partitioning, consumer groups, parallelism up to your partition count

title: Principal Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About Sezzle: 

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

Compensation :

For this principal development role, with 12+ years of experience, the compensation range is $12,500 - $20,800 USD based on location and experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the extensive expertise, leadership capabilities, and significant contributions expected at this level, offering a competitive salary to reflect the value of advanced skills and experience

About the Role: 

We are seeking an exceptional Principal Infrastructure Engineer to design, build, operate, and scale the platform that powers Sezzle. Your focus will be the hardest infrastructure problems: increasing throughput, reducing latency, removing capacity bottlenecks, strengthening resilience, and making production operations more automated and predictable as the business grows.

You will own complex technical initiatives from architecture and prototyping through implementation, production rollout, and ongoing operation. Your impact will come from the systems you build, the problems you solve, and measurable improvements in reliability, performance, and cost efficiency.

Our stack runs on AWS , with workloads orchestrated on Kubernetes and data anchored in Aurora RDS (MySQL and Postgres) . You should know these technologies deeply and be comfortable moving between cloud architecture, networking, cluster internals, database performance, and application behavior to understand how the entire system scales. You will write code and infrastructure-as-code, debug production systems, and deliver changes that hold up under real traffic and failure conditions.

Operational ownership is part of the job. You will participate in the on-call rotation and take a hands-on role in recovering from major incidents, including full outages. We need someone who can form and test hypotheses using logs, metrics, and traces, make sound mitigation decisions with incomplete information, and turn incident findings into lasting engineering fixes.

You will also build and apply AI-assisted infrastructure and SRE tooling for incident investigation, capacity analysis, runbook automation, and toil reduction. You will evaluate these tools through practical results and apply appropriate access controls, validation, and auditability to their use in production.

This role reports to engineering leadership and works closely with application engineers, Security, and Compliance. You will develop a deep understanding of how Sezzle's business operates and how customer journeys, transaction patterns, and product decisions shape infrastructure demand and behavior. You will use that understanding to identify and deliver improvements across teams and technical domains, connecting infrastructure decisions to better customer outcomes and business performance.

What you’ll do: 

- Own the technical architecture and evolution of core infrastructure : identify system limits, prioritize technical improvements, and implement changes that support increasing traffic, data volume, and workload complexity.

- Connect business understanding to improvements across the system : learn how key business workflows behave in production, trace their impact across applications, data, and infrastructure, and partner across teams to improve performance, reliability, and cost efficiency beyond any single service or team's scope.

- Engineer for scale and performance : build capacity models, run load and stress tests, diagnose bottlenecks across compute, networking, Kubernetes, and databases, and validate improvements against throughput, latency, saturation, and cost per workload.

- Design and build AWS infrastructure : implement resilient account, IAM, network, and service architectures; address service quotas, fault isolation, and multi-AZ or multi-region requirements as workloads grow.

- Build and operate the Kubernetes platform : improve cluster architecture, lifecycle automation, workload isolation, resource allocation, autoscaling, safe upgrades, and deployment reliability.

- Scale and optimize Aurora RDS for MySQL and Postgres : tune queries and indexes, address connection and replication bottlenecks, plan capacity, improve failover behavior, and implement safe schema changes and database migrations with application engineers.

- Improve reliability through engineering : define and instrument service-level objectives and error budgets with service owners; implement failure isolation, backpressure, load shedding, and safe retry behavior where needed to prevent cascading failures.

- Participate in on-call and drive technical recovery during serious incidents : use evidence-based triage, execute mitigations, communicate findings, and implement corrective actions from postmortems.

- Implement and test disaster recovery : design backup, restore, and failover mechanisms against agreed recovery time and recovery point objectives; run recovery exercises and document measured results.

- Build infrastructure-as-code and operational automation : make provisioning, configuration, deployments, upgrades, and recovery reproducible, reviewed, testable, and recoverable. Eliminate recurring manual work through code.

- Build observability that makes production diagnosable : improve metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and actionable alerts, with visibility into service health, scaling limits, and customer impact.

- Deliver safe infrastructure migrations : design phased rollouts, compatibility checks, validation, and rollback paths for changes to shared production systems.

- Improve cloud cost efficiency through technical changes : right-size resources, improve utilization, tune autoscaling and storage, and quantify savings while maintaining reliability and performance targets.

- Build and evaluate AI-assisted operational tooling : apply AI to investigation, runbooks, anomaly analysis, and repetitive operations, with bounded permissions, reviewable actions, and measurable improvements in accuracy or toil.

- Make technical decisions clear and executable : write architecture proposals, evaluate technology tradeoffs through prototypes and benchmarks, review changes affecting shared infrastructure, and document how systems operate and fail.

What We look for: 

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a similar technical field (required)

- 12+ years of experience across infrastructure, platform, site reliability, software development, or related engineering disciplines, with substantial hands-on depth designing and operating production infrastructure at scale.

- Deep expertise with AWS : production experience across compute, IAM, multi-account architectures, and networking, including VPC design and private connectivity.

- Deep expertise with Kubernetes in production : cluster lifecycle, scheduling, resource management, autoscaling, networking, and troubleshooting business-critical workloads. EKS experience is strongly preferred.

- Deep expertise with relational databases at scale , specifically RDS/Aurora (MySQL and/or Postgres) : query performance, indexing, connection management, replication, high availability, failover, and verified backup and recovery.

- A track record of personally delivering infrastructure scaling improvements : identifying constraints, measuring baseline behavior, implementing changes, and demonstrating gains in capacity, latency, reliability, or cost efficiency.

- Strong coding and automation skills , using Golang, Python, or similar languages to build production tooling and eliminate operational toil, alongside infrastructure-as-code experience with Terraform or equivalent.

- Strong systems fundamentals : Linux, networking, DNS, TLS, storage, concurrency, and distributed system failure modes, with the ability to debug problems across infrastructure and application boundaries.

- Experience operating a 24/7, high-availability platform where downtime has direct customer or revenue impact, including hands-on incident response and postmortem remediation.

- Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation and demonstrated ability to recover production systems under pressure using evidence-based triage, safe mitigation, and clear technical communication.

- Experience implementing and testing disaster recovery against defined recovery objectives, including restoring data and validating service recovery.

- Practical experience with observability, load testing, capacity planning, and safe CI/CD practices for shared production infrastructure.

- Active use of AI tooling in engineering or operations , with practical judgment about its limitations and how to verify generated code, recommendations, and operational actions.

- Ability to carry ambiguous technical problems from investigation through production delivery and collaborate across engineering disciplines to resolve system-wide constraints.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills: 

- Experience in fintech, payments, or banking , operating infrastructure with demanding reliability, security, and audit requirements.

- Experience with multi-region architectures, chaos engineering, and failure testing , including the consistency and recovery tradeoffs of distributed data systems.

- Proficiency with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo , or comparable observability systems.

- Experience building internal platform capabilities and self-service tooling , including deployment automation, progressive delivery, and reusable infrastructure components.

- Experience building AI-assisted incident investigation or operational automation with restricted access, auditable execution, and clear human review points

About You:

- You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things

title: Senior OSINT Data Analyst
description:
Datenna is a fast-growing tech scale-up combining cutting-edge OSINT and AI technologies to provide governments with critical insights into China's techno-economic landscape. Our platform transforms open-source intelligence into actionable insights through advanced data processing and analysis. 

The Role: As Senior OSINT Data Analyst you will sit at the core of Datenna’s product operations and act as a domain authority for our data. You will define which foreign-language sources we collect for each region we cover, set and defend the standards that data is held to, and turn complex registry, procurement, and patent material into structured, platform-ready intelligence. You will own major areas of coverage end to end, guide the analysts around you, and be a trusted voice in product decisions. 

Your mission at Datenna:

Analysis and data intelligence 

- Apply deep regional domain knowledge to develop products that identify, map, and classify entities across corporate, academic, defence-industrial, and innovation landscapes, with a focus on state-military-commercial integration, dual-use technologies, state ownership, and technology transfer. 

- Use pattern-recognition skills to connect corporate, state, and military actors, including opaque ownership structures and intermediaries, and generate structured intelligence that feeds directly into Datenna’s platform. 

- Make and defend analytical judgements on entity risk labelling, ownership mapping, and procurement tracking, prioritising platform-ready outputs over long-form research deliverables. 

Data Collection, quality and lifecycle management 

- Define and own data collection workstreams end to end: identifying, evaluating, and extracting structured information from non-English sources including corporate registries, procurement portals, patent databases, academic repositories, and state media. 

- Manage data across its full lifecycle, from initial acquisition and parsing through cleaning, enrichment, validation, and delivery into Datenna’s platform, maintaining rigorous standards so that every data point is traceable, accurate, and defensible. 

- Work closely with the Data Lead to set and continuously refine data quality benchmarks, turning observations from collection and testing work into improvements to automated pipelines. 

Product development 

- Play a leading role in Datenna’s data-driven product development cycle, contributing regional domain expertise to the design, testing, and refinement of new platform features and data products. 

- Shape how Datenna’s proprietary risk labelling systems evolve, drawing on hands-on OSINT experience to identify edge cases and improve classification accuracy. 

- Map gaps in Datenna’s data coverage against what customers need, and make the case for the sources, methods, and investment required to close them, including the extension of our approach to new regions. 

Coordination and collaboration 

- Coordinate between data researchers and software developers to support smooth data processing pipelines, translating analytical requirements into clear technical specifications. 

- Set the methodological standard for OSINT work as the team grows: reviewing outputs, mentoring junior and medior researchers on OSINT tradecraft, and ensuring work meets Datenna’s data quality standards. 

What makes you a great candidate: 

- 8-10 years of hands-on OSINT experience, including direct collection, verification, and analysis from non-English open sources such as corporate registries, government procurement portals, patent databases, academic repositories, and state media. 

- Demonstrable experience contributing to data-driven product development, whether through structured dataset creation, analytical input into software features, or validation of intelligence platform outputs. 

- Reading proficiency in Chinese at minimum HSK 4 level or equivalent, together with the ability to independently source, interrogate, and extract structured data from foreign-language materials. Working proficiency in Russian is preferred. 

- Strong knowledge of at least one region’s corporate sector, innovation ecosystem, defence-industrial base, industrial policy, and the intersection of state, military, and commercial actors, with the ability to identify entity-level connections across Datenna’s key domains and to learn new jurisdictions quickly. 

- Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methods, with experience producing analytical outputs for non-specialist audiences and presenting findings to customers or senior stakeholders. 

- Familiarity with data analysis tools such as Python, R, or SQL, and comfort working with large structured datasets and contributing to data pipelines. Experience with name-matching and transliteration at scale, for example Chinese or Cyrillic, is an advantage. 

- A postgraduate qualification in Area Studies, International Relations, Security Studies, or a related field is preferred. 

*Please know that applicants may be subject to a screening process.* 

AI is part of how we build 

We use AI tools extensively to move faster and raise quality, and we focus our human attention on the work where judgment, creativity, and responsibility matter most. We expect every candidate to be comfortable using AI in their day-to-day work in a responsible manner and to continuously look for better ways to apply it.

- Lead innovation in OSINT and AI technologies 

- Competitive compensation and benefits 

- Dynamic, international team environment 

- Significant growth opportunities in a scale-up 

When you apply to this position, we will process your personal data according to our Recruitment Privacy Notice .

Job Description: 

The Resident Director is responsible for the successful operational delivery of all WorldStrides programs in Amsterdam. The role involves oversight of student services, faculty-led program operations, financial administration, health and safety, local partnerships, and strategic development. 

The Resident Director serves as the primary local representative of WorldStrides and plays a key role in ensuring an outstanding experience for students, faculty, and institutional partners.

- Plan and coordinate educational itineraries and program schedules.

- Arrange accommodations, transportation, restaurant bookings, and local services. 

- Confirm operational services and requirements with suppliers.

- Liaise with faculty before, during, and after programs. Coordinate participant communications. 

- Manage operational changes and troubleshoot issues as they arise. 

- Support on-site program delivery when required. 

- Conduct post-program reviews and evaluations. 

- Identify opportunities for operational improvement and efficiency. 

2) Individual (Study Abroad) Programs 
Responsible for supporting students throughout their study abroad experience at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (Fall, Spring and Summer sessions) 

- Coordinate student arrivals and departures. 

- Arrange and oversee airport transfers. 

- Deliver and coordinate orientation programs (BCO).

title: Traineeship Aftersales Servicecontracten
Afstudeerstage IT
description:
Bij BAS, Europa’s grootste dealer in commerciële voertuigen én officieel Volvo en Renault Trucks dealer, krijg jij de kans om je te ontwikkelen binnen IT in de automotive branche. Ben jij op zoek naar een afstudeerstage vanaf januari/ februari 2027? Dan is dit iets voor jou!

BAS World groeit hard, en IT speelt daarin een sleutelrol. Binnen ons IT-team liggen verschillende afstudeeropdrachten klaar die elk een echt vraagstuk uit ons IT-landschap aanpakken. Elke opdracht heeft een eigen team dat je dagelijks begeleidt. Zo breng je je kennis in de praktijk en kickstart je samen met ons jouw carrière.

Mogelijke afstudeeropdrachten

1. Continuous performance & load testing (Engineering) 
BAS World wil het aantal voertuigadvertenties online ongeveer 20 keer zo groot maken. In deze opdracht zorg je dat onze websites en systemen die groei aankunnen. Je onderzoekt welke (AI-gedreven) testtools passen bij onze stack. Daarna bouw je samen met het IDP-team een testsuite die dagelijks automatisch draait in de pipeline. Het resultaat is een productieklare testopzet en een advies over knelpunten en capaciteit.
Past bij: Software Engineering, DevOps, Infrastructure. 

2. Kleine AI-agents voor de business (Data / AI engineering) 
In deze opdracht werk je als interne consultant binnen één afdeling, bijvoorbeeld Logistiek. Je spreekt gebruikers, brengt hun processen en knelpunten in kaart en bepaalt waar AI het meeste oplevert. Daarna bouw je één of meer kleine AI-agents op basis van de services en data die we al hebben. Je test ze en verbetert ze tot ze echt gebruikt worden in het dagelijkse werk.
Past bij: AI, Data Science, Business IT, Software Engineering, als je graag dicht op eindgebruikers werkt. 

3. Realtime monitoring & bottleneck-analyse voor Thinkwise-applicaties (Engineering) 
Verschillende kernapplicaties draaien op het low-code platform Thinkwise. Als gebruikers traagheid melden, kost het nu weken om de oorzaak te vinden. In deze opdracht bouw je monitoring die de performance over de hele stack realtime inzichtelijk maakt: van UI en applicatielaag tot database en netwerk. Die performance komt live op een scherm op de werkvloer van onze developers. Daarnaast ontwikkel je rapportage- en analysetooling waarmee developers bottlenecks precies kunnen aanwijzen en oplossen waar ze ontstaan. Zo vinden we problemen in uren in plaats van weken.
Past bij: Software Engineering, Infrastructure, DevOps, met interesse in performance en observability. 

4. Problem management & ITSM-procesoptimalisatie (System & Application Management) 
Onze Servicedesk en het S&AM-team krijgen veel meldingen binnen in Jira. Terugkerende problemen worden nog te weinig bij de bron opgelost. In deze opdracht breng je de ITSM-processen in kaart en leg je ze vast: processtromen, werkinstructies en rollen. Je toetst ze aan good practices zoals ITIL. Daarna ontwerp en implementeer je problem management als een vast proces, zodat terugkerende issues structureel verdwijnen.
Past bij: Business IT & Management, IT Service Management of verwant. 

5. Datagedreven leadgeneratie met FleetCareXL & BAS World (Product) 
Via FleetCareXL weten we precies hoe voertuigen onderhouden worden en wat dat kost. De verkoophistorie van BAS World vertelt ons veel over restwaardes. In deze opdracht combineer je deze twee databronnen in een proof of concept. Die berekent het ideale vervangmoment: wanneer onderhoudskosten gaan stijgen terwijl de restwaarde nog hoog is. Dat levert kostenbesparing op voor klanten en leads voor in- en verkoop. De opdracht kan ook andersom worden ingevuld. Dan onderzoek je hoe we FleetGuide selfservice of fullservice actief kunnen aanbieden aan klanten van BAS World.
Past bij: Data Science, Business Analytics, Software Engineering, met commerciële interesse. 

Kortom: veel verantwoordelijkheid, veel samenwerking en een opdracht met echte impact.

Wij bieden jou

- Een stagevergoeding van €500,- bruto per maand voor een fulltime stage én reiskostenvergoeding ;

- Een inhoudelijke en uitdagende afstudeeropdracht met zichtbare impact;

- Dagelijkse begeleiding vanuit het team dat jouw opdracht host;

- De mogelijkheid om onderdeel uit te maken van ons gedreven en enthousiaste IT-team;

- Bij goede prestaties uitzicht op een vaste functie binnen BAS . Bij BAS zeggen we namelijk niet voor niets: “Bij BAS heb je geen baan maar een carrière!”;

- Een vaste kruk bij de VrijMiBo en jouw naam op de gastenlijst voor onze bedrijfsuitjes en feestjes.

- Je volgt een HBO-opleiding richting Software Engineering, DevOps, Data Science, AI, Business IT & Management, IT Service Management of een gerelateerde opleiding;

- Je vindt het leuk om systemen en processen te verbeteren en oplossingen te bouwen die echt gebruikt worden;

- Je bent nieuwsgierig en hebt de drive om te leren en jezelf te ontwikkelen.

Wij zijn BAS!

We zijn actief sinds 1962. Sindsdien vestigden wij onze naam als een betrouwbare kracht in de Automotive. Als familiebedrijf zijn wij wereldwijd actief in kopen, onderhouden en verkopen van vrachtwagens, trekkers, trailers, bouwmachines, bedrijfswagens en landbouwmachines.

Al onze kennis en ervaring verwerkten we daarnaast in de ontwikkeling van basworld.com. Hier verbinden we kopers en verkopers met elkaar en helpen we hen om snel, gemakkelijk en veilig te handelen. Onze ambitie voor BAS kent geen grenzen. Rijd jij voorop om BAS naar het volgende niveau te brengen?

Samengevat: bij BAS gaan we altijd vol gas en is geen dag hetzelfde. Met meer dan 1.000 collega’s proberen wij onszelf iedere dag een stukje beter te maken voor onze klanten. Daarbij staan Brabantse nuchterheid, passie, teamwork en ondernemerschap voorop.

- Samenwerking met ervaren collega’s, leveranciers en contractors,
- Een werkomgeving waarin veiligheid, eigenaarschap en continue verbetering centraal staan.

NORIT heeft een geschiedenis van 100 jaar in het innoveren en ontwikkelen van actieve kool voor diverse toepassingen. Wij helpen bedrijven, gemeenten en eindgebruikers te genieten van schonere en veiligere productie. title: Mission Systems Engineer (m/w/d) / Space & Defense Industry
description:
About the Company

Infinite Orbits GmbH is the German subsidiary of Infinite Orbits SAS, a NewSpace company founded in 2017 that now has more than 200 employees, with locations including Luxembourg, the UK, Spain, and Singapore.

The company develops in-orbit servicing solutions built on its own autonomous Rendezvous and Proximity Operations (RPO) technology, spanning awareness, surveillance, inspection, and protection of space assets through to life extension.

With its newly established Munich site, Infinite Orbits builds a dedicated local presence in Germany, developing capabilities in business development, R&D, product development, system engineering, production, and mission operations to enable Europe's defense and space sector.

About the Role

As Mission Systems Engineer, you own the mission. You turn customer needs into feasible, defensible mission concepts for RPO and in-orbit servicing across space segment, ground segment, launch, operations, and user segment, and you define the requirements each segment has to meet.

Proposal preparation is at the core of this role: you lead the technical volume of Infinite Orbits Germany's bids and RFI/RFP responses and provide the mission content for funding applications, from the first mission sketch to the submitted document. Working hand in hand with Business Development and the Proposal & Project Manager, you shape the technical solution that qualifies an opportunity and wins it, building on proven product and technology solutions from Engineering in Toulouse and other Group entities.

Once contracts are won, you carry your mission concept into execution. As a founding technical hire, you own the analysis that underpins every German proposal and delivery.

Job Description

- Technical proposal lead: Lead the technical volume of RFI/RFP responses and customer proposals and provide mission content for national and European funding applications: mission concept, solution description, feasibility evidence, and technical risks and mitigations. Provide technical input to the compliance matrix, work breakdown structure, schedule, and cost, which the Proposal & Project Manager owns.

- Bid strategy & win themes: Work with Business Development and the Proposal & Project Manager on bid/no-bid decisions, win themes, and technical discriminators; drive technical reviews and answer clarification questions through to submission.

- Mission analysis ownership: Own RPO and in-orbit servicing mission analysis, including orbit and trajectory design, approach and abort strategies, safety and collision-avoidance concepts, and Δv and timeline budgets.

- Mission concept & ConOps: Define mission architectures and concepts of operations across all mission phases, from launch and early operations through to end of life.

- Requirements & allocation: Derive mission requirements from customer needs and allocate them to space segment, ground segment, launch, and operations; define the spacecraft-level requirements baseline together with the Satellite Systems Engineer.

- End-to-end trade-offs: Run and document system-level trade-offs, ensuring technical coherence across all segments.

- Sales & business development support: Provide technical depth in early customer conversations and capability presentations, and qualify new opportunities with Business Development.

- Project execution: Own technical workstreams on won contracts, in particular concept and feasibility studies (Phase 0/A), ensuring delivery against mission and contractual requirements.

- Group coordination: Work with Engineering in Toulouse and other Group entities to align mission analysis methods and leverage existing product and technology solutions across the Infinite Orbits Group.

Requirements

Education & Experience

- Engineering degree in aerospace, astrodynamics, space systems engineering, or a related field, or equivalent.

- 3+ years of experience in mission analysis or mission systems engineering, with a track record of independently owning technical workstreams.

- Hands-on experience preparing technical proposals, study proposals, or funding applications in the space or defense sector (e.g. ESA, DLR, Bundeswehr, EU).

- Experience with RPO, GNC, formation flying, or in-orbit servicing missions is a strong plus.

Skills & Other Requirements

- Strong command of mission analysis tools and methods (e.g. STK, GMAT, Orekit, Python).

- Working knowledge across space segment, ground segment, launcher interfaces, and user segment integration.

- Ability to size, defend, and iterate mission solutions under customer or stakeholder scrutiny.

- Excellent structured writing: able to turn technical analysis into compelling, compliant proposal content under deadline pressure.

- Comfortable engaging directly with customers and prospects to support sales and business development conversations.

- Autonomy and ownership: comfortable owning workstreams independently in an early-stage, cross-border team environment, working closely with Group entities in France and beyond.

- Fluent in German and English.

- Willingness to undergo a German security clearance procedure (Sicherheitsüberprüfung).

- Frequent travel required within Germany and to Infinite Orbits' HQ in Toulouse and other European locations.

What we offer

- A founding technical role with direct ownership of mission concepts and technical proposals in a growing European space and defense company.

- Direct exposure to customers, bids, and cross-border collaboration with the Infinite Orbits Group.

WE ARE LOOKING FORWARD TO YOUR APPLICATION!

title: Embedded Software Entwickler (m/w/d)
description:
Du möchtest nicht nur Software entwickeln, sondern direkt erleben, wie dein Code reale Systeme steuert und weiterentwickelt ? 

Dann könnte diese Position genau das Richtige für dich sein. 

Unser Kunde entwickelt und fertigt autonome Drohnensysteme, Einsatzsoftware und spezialisierte Lösungen für Industrie, Netzbetreiber, Behörden und maritime Anwendungen. Dabei entstehen hochspezialisierte Systeme, die Hardware, Software und autonome Technologien miteinander verbinden und bereits bei namhaften Kunden zum Einsatz kommen. 

Für die Weiterentwicklung der Drohnensysteme wird eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit gesucht, die Verantwortung für hardwarenahe Software übernimmt, bestehende Systeme weiterentwickelt und gemeinsam mit einem kleinen technischen Team neue Funktionen bis zum Flugtest bringt. 

Deine Benefits

- Attraktive Vergütung: Ein leistungsgerechtes Fixgehalt, das deiner Erfahrung und Qualifikation entspricht. 

- Gestaltungsspielraum: Hohe Eigenverantwortung bei der Weiterentwicklung zentraler Softwarekomponenten und technischen Strukturen. 

- Entwicklungsperspektive: Perspektivisch besteht die Möglichkeit, fachliche Verantwortung für das Softwareteam zu übernehmen. 

- Technologieumfeld: Arbeit an innovativen Drohnensystemen, Embedded Software und autonomen Technologien mit direktem Bezug zur Hardware. 

- Praxisnähe: Kurze Wege von der Entwicklung zum Flugtest und die Möglichkeit, neue Funktionen direkt im realen System zu erproben. 

- Flexibilität: Nach der Einarbeitung ist Homeoffice nach Absprache möglich, wobei die regelmäßige Arbeit an Hardware eine Präsenz vor Ort erforderlich macht. 

- Arbeitsumfeld: Eigene Werkstatt und Testgelände sowie moderne Hard und Software für die Entwicklung und Erprobung. 

- Unternehmenskultur: Kurze Entscheidungswege, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und eine offene Du Kultur. 

- Teamspirit: Regelmäßige gemeinsame Aktivitäten und Teamevents sorgen für ein persönliches und unkompliziertes Miteinander. 

- Individuelle Benefits: Persönliche Wünsche und Vorschläge sind willkommen. Gemeinsam werden individuelle Benefits erarbeitet. 

Deine Aufgaben

Als Embedded Software Entwickler übernimmst du eine zentrale Rolle bei der Weiterentwicklung der Flugsteuerungs- und Bedienersoftware unserer Drohnensysteme. 

- Flight Control: Technische Verantwortung für die Weiterentwicklung der Flugsteuerungssoftware und deren zuverlässigen Betrieb auf der Zielhardware. 

- Bodenkontrollsoftware: Weiterentwicklung einer modernen Bedienersoftware auf Basis von Qt und QML für Missionsplanung, Drohnenüberwachung und Nutzlaststeuerung. 

- Codebasis: Einarbeitung in bestehende Softwarestrukturen, Dokumentation der Architektur sowie Aufbau sauberer Prozesse für Tests, Releases und Updates. 

- Hardwareintegration: Anbindung und Integration von Sensoren, Funkmodulen, Kameras, Ladesystemen und weiteren Nutzlasten. 

- Debugging: Analyse von Fluglogs, Auswertung technischer Daten und systematische Fehlersuche direkt auf der Zielhardware. 

- Flugerprobung: Begleitung und Durchführung von Flugtests sowie technische Unterstützung bei Erprobungen und gelegentlichen Kundeneinsätzen. 

- Technische Leitung: Fachliche Betreuung eines Auszubildenden und von Werkstudenten, Durchführung von Code Reviews und aktive Weitergabe von Wissen. 

- Architektur: Mitarbeit an technischen Architekturentscheidungen in enger Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung. 

- Zusammenarbeit: Enge Abstimmung mit Hardwareentwicklung, Konstruktion und Werkstatt, um Software und Gesamtsystem gemeinsam weiterzuentwickeln. 

Dein Profil

- Mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung, davon überwiegend im Embedded Bereich oder in der hardwarenahen C und C++ Entwicklung. 

- Sehr gute praktische Kenntnisse in modernem C++, Qt und QML . Sowie Linux und Git. 

- Erfahrung darin, sich selbstständig in umfangreiche bestehende Codebasen einzuarbeiten und komplexe Softwarestrukturen schnell zu verstehen. 

- Fundierte Erfahrung im hardwarenahen Debugging , insbesondere mit Sensoren, Schnittstellen wie UART, CAN, SPI oder I2C sowie der Analyse von Logs und Fehlerbildern auf Zielhardware. 

- Strukturierte und eigenständige Arbeitsweise sowie die Bereitschaft, technische Lösungen und Wissen nachvollziehbar zu dokumentieren und weiterzugeben. 

- Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit Hardwareentwicklung und technischen Fachbereichen sowie Interesse daran, Software direkt am realen System zu testen. 

- Bereitschaft zur regelmäßigen Arbeit vor Ort sowie zur Teilnahme an Flugtests und gelegentlichen Kundeneinsätzen. 

- Fließende Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse 

Nice to have 

- Kenntnisse in ArduPilot oder PX4, MAVLink oder DroneCAN. 

- Wissen in Regelungstechnik, Zustandsschätzung oder Navigation, beispielsweise mit EKF, GNSS oder RTK. 

- Erfahrung mit Open Source Projekten und ein entsprechendes GitHub Profil. 

- Erste Erfahrung als technischer Lead oder im Mentoring jüngerer Entwickler. 

- Erfahrung mit Luftfahrt oder Verteidigungsprojekten sowie Kenntnisse relevanter Safety Standards. 

- Praktische Drohnen Flugerfahrung oder EU Kompetenznachweis A1/A3 beziehungsweise A2.

Klingt nach deiner nächsten Herausforderung? 

Wenn du Embedded Software nicht nur entwickeln, sondern direkt in innovativen Drohnensystemen zum Einsatz bringen möchtest und dabei echte technische Verantwortung übernehmen willst, freuen wir uns auf deinen Lebenslauf. 

In einem kurzen, unverbindlichen Telefonat geben wir dir anschließend alle weiteren Informationen zur Position und zum Unternehmen.

title: IT Systemadministrator
description:
Deine Benefits

- Verantwortung: Als zentrale IT-Ansprechperson übernimmst du Verantwortung für das technische Rückgrat des Unternehmens.

- Ausstattung: Moderne Hardware und die notwendige technische Ausstattung für deine tägliche Arbeit.

- Unternehmenskultur: Kurze Entscheidungswege, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und eine offene Du Kultur.

Deine Aufgaben

Als IT Systemadministrator verantwortest du den zuverlässigen Betrieb und die Weiterentwicklung der internen IT-Infrastruktur.

- Server & Virtualisierung: Betreuung und Administration der Windows Server Umgebung sowie der eingesetzten virtuellen Maschinen.

- Infrastruktur: Betreuung und Weiterentwicklung von WLAN, Firewall und weiteren zentralen Komponenten der IT-Infrastruktur.

- Benutzerverwaltung: Administration von Nutzern, Gruppen und Berechtigungen im Active Directory.

- Servertausch: Mitarbeit beim geplanten Austausch der bestehenden Serverlandschaft und aktive Mitgestaltung der neuen Infrastruktur.

- IT Sicherheit: Kontinuierliche Überprüfung und Verbesserung der technischen Sicherheitsstandards.

- Hardware & Lizenzen: Beschaffung, Einrichtung und Verwaltung von Hardware sowie Betreuung des Lizenzmanagements.

- Support: Unterstützung der Mitarbeitenden bei technischen Fragen und Problemen im Arbeitsalltag.

Dein Profil

- Min. 5 Jahre praktische Erfahrung in der IT Systemadministration, idealerweise mit eigenständiger Betreuung von IT Umgebungen.

- Sehr gute Kenntnisse in der Administration von Windows Servern und virtuellen Maschinen.

- Erfahrung mit Active Directory sowie der Verwaltung von Nutzern, Gruppen und Berechtigungen.

- Praxis in der Administration von Firewalls und grundlegenden Netzwerkkomponenten.

- Die Fähigkeit, eine kleinere Unternehmens IT eigenständig zu betreuen und technische Probleme strukturiert zu lösen.

- Selbstständige und verantwortungsbewusste Arbeitsweise mit dem Anspruch, Themen eigenständig zu erkennen und umzusetzen.

- Idealerweise abgeschlossenes Studium oder vergleichbare Qualifikation im IT Bereich.

- Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichen-Niveau und gute Englischkenntnisse

Nice to have

- Erfahrung mit VPN Lösungen und deren Konfiguration und Administration.

- Kenntnisse im Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

- Zusätzliches Know-How im Bereich IT Security.

title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
description:
Your Mission

This is a company built for growth, not comfort. 

When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone. 

We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences. 

Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in. 

If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you. 

What You’ll Own:

- Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.

- Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.

- Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.

- Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.

- Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.

- Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.

- Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

- You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.

- Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.

- Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.

- Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.

- You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.

- You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

- Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.

- Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.

- Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.

- Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.

- Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.

- Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.

- Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.

- Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

- Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.

- Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.

- See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.

- Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.

- Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

title: Country Executive
description:
The finance function is broken. Everyone building for it is boring.

Fast-growing multi-entity companies get two options: duct-tape a Frankenstack, or surrender to a corporate ERP and its consultant army. Both are bad. Both are beatable. Beating them market by market is this job.

Light is the AI-native financial platform for modern companies. Fast to implement, intuitive to use, smarter every month. We call it organic software. Legora, Lovable, and Fuse Energy run on it. Product ships something worth shouting about every single week.

What we don't have is a single person on the ground in your country.

THIS IS NOT A COUNTRY MANAGER ROLE.

Most first-in-market hires get a quota, a deck, and a flight. They repeat the London pitch in a local accent and forward complaints to HQ. This is the opposite. This is a founding hire for someone who wants far more scope than their years of experience would get them anywhere else.

No entity. No local team. No local playbook. You are Light's first boots on the ground in your market, and within a year you should know that market's complexity - its rules, its buyers, its excuses - better than anyone else. It's not a leadership title. It's the seed of one. Do this right and there's a real path: stand up an entity, hire a team around you, move into product, or run the region as GM.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING.

- Sitting across from finance leaders. Real conversations, not discovery calls off a script. You find out what they actually need - the thing behind the thing they asked for - and you come back with it written down clearly enough for engineers to build against.

- Being the connective tissue. Customer, product, commercial. What you learn in-market changes how Light builds and how Light sells. You are the wire between them, and the wire has to carry current in both directions.

- Owning the local rulebook. Compliance, regulation, filing, the specific ways finance is done badly in your country. You're the person in the room who genuinely knows this, and you make sure it shows up in the product and in the pitch.

- Having a public point of view. Ideally you arrive with a finance background and an opinion on what "doing finance right" looks like here. Bring it into the market, into the roadmap, and into how every prospect sees Light. Relationships, events, brand presence - built from zero, by you.

- Closing, with London behind you. Our sales team helps you manage and push deals over the line. You bring the market and customer understanding that makes those conversations land. They support you; they don't carry you and you don't carry it alone.

HOW WE'LL KEEP SCORE.

This isn't a pure revenue seat, but growing your country's ARR is the primary goal and you're tied directly to that number. A starting point will be set on what you're measured against on day one and you have to prove your worth.

WHAT WE'LL ASK FOR.

- The thing you built from nothing. A company, a market, a GTM motion, a product. Something that existed because you hacked through a messy sale with no playbook. First question in the first call.

- Credibility in front of a CFO. A finance background ideally, or enough substance that a finance leader takes you seriously the moment you walk in. You can't be the voice of the market without an ear for the buyer.

- 2+ years as a founder or co-founder. Ex-founder or very early operator. We want the scar tissue.

- 6+ years somewhere fast. High-growth tech, top-tier strategy consulting, investment banking, or similar. Or a body of work that makes the number irrelevant.

- Structured thinking under mess. Exceptional analytical instincts, applied to markets nobody has mapped for you yet.

- Fluency in your market's language and in English. Both, properly.

Extra credit: exposure to accounting, enterprise software, fintech or SaaS as a user, buyer or advisor; time spent presenting to senior finance stakeholders; an existing finance network in your market - or a demonstrated, unembarrassed intent to build one.

THE GOOD STUFF.

💸 Competitive salary plus potential stock options.
🏝 25 days annual leave plus public holidays where you're based.
🚀 A genuine chance to build a market from the ground up and grow with it.
🥳 Regular socials and company off-sites - the last one was in Italy.
🌍 Time with the team in London, Copenhagen, Munich, NY, Paris and wherever the action is.

HOW TO APPLY.

Show us who you are, not just your CV. Tell us what you built and what it did in numbers. Then answer the only question that matters: why this one? Anyone can say they want to work at a startup. A generic AI-written cover letter with no craft behind the prompt will be obvious - and is its own kind of answer.

If this reads as too much scope for one person: it is. That's the seat.

Just one year after our founding, Artemis is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies of all time, with customers including multiple Fortune 500 companies, Global 2000 enterprises, and AI innovators like Cursor.

We have raised $70M from Felicis, First Round Capital, Theory Ventures, Two Sigma Ventures, Lockstep VC and Brightmind. We are also backed by some of the most prominent operators in cybersecurity, including the CEO of Crowdstrike, the former CEO and CTO of Splunk, and the founders of Abnormal AI and Demisto.

Artemis's founders have built and scaled security products used by tens of thousands of customers. Shachar Hirshberg (CEO) led Amazon GuardDuty, the world's largest cloud detection product, was an early employee at Demisto, the company that invented the SOAR category, was an engineering leader at Palo Alto Networks, and holds an MBA from Harvard. Dan Shiebler (CTO) led all AI and machine learning at Abnormal AI, the pioneer of behavior-based detection, spent five years building analytics using machine learning and vector databases at Twitter, and holds a PhD in machine learning from Oxford.

Our team of software engineers, AI researchers, security engineers, and product designers comes from Google, Meta, AWS, Wiz, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Abnormal AI, Perplexity, Bridgewater, Mercor, CERN, and more.

We're growing fast and looking for builders who want to help us serve our rapidly expanding customer base.

Job Overview 

As Enterprise Account Executive, you'll own enterprise revenue from day one. You'll build our pipeline, develop strategic relationships with security executives, and close deals that prove our value in market. You'll work directly with our founders to shape not just revenue, but how we position, package, and sell our platform to security-conscious enterprises.

This role combines the autonomy and equity upside of a startup with the backing of proven partnerships and a category-defining product. You'll have an unparalleled impact on our go-to-market trajectory and build the foundation for the sales organization we'll scale around you.

Responsibilities 

- Develop and execute territory plans targeting Fortune 1000 and Global 2000 security organizations. You'll identify and prioritize accounts where Artemis delivers the most strategic value, building multi-threaded relationships from security operations teams through the CISO.

- Build a qualified pipeline through strategic outbound prospecting and industry engagement. This is all about creating opportunities.

- Lead complex, consultative sales cycles. You'll articulate how AI-driven defense changes the economics and effectiveness of their security programs.

- Collaborate with our technical team to deliver compelling proofs-of-concept and technical evaluations. You'll navigate technical objections, competitive positioning, and architecture discussions alongside our founders.

- Drive accurate forecasting and maintain rigorous pipeline hygiene in HubSpot. You'll own the forecast and build the discipline that scales with future hires.

- Represent Artemis at key industry events.

- Serve as voice of customer, providing strategic feedback to our founders and team. Your insights from the field will directly shape our roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

- Document and refine our sales methodology to enable future team growth.

Qualifications 

- Proven experience selling enterprise cybersecurity solutions. 7+ years of enterprise sales experience with consistent over-achievement (120%+ quota attainment). You've sold into Fortune 1000 and Global 2000 security organizations with deal sizes of $250K-$1M+ and know how to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder buying processes.

- Deep understanding of enterprise security architectures and the CISO buying journey . You speak fluently about detection, response, AI/ML in security, and can hold your own in technical conversations about data platforms, SIEM, EDR/XDR, and cloud security.

- Established relationships with enterprise CISOs, security leaders, and security operations teams . You have credibility in the market and know how to leverage it.

- Track record of building pipeline without heavy marketing support . You're a hunter who thrives on ecosystem leverage and creating your own opportunities.

- Strong executive presence and ability to command both technical and business conversations. You can shift seamlessly between ROI discussions and architecture talks with the security engineering team.

- Proficiency in value-based selling and solution-selling methodologies (such as MEDDICC).

- Experience leveraging channel partners and strategic alliances to accelerate deals . You understand how to work the ecosystem.

- Expert-level use of HubSpot and a disciplined approach to pipeline management. You've built forecasts that executives trust.

Preferred: 

- Experience at high-growth, early-stage cybersecurity companies (Series A-B) where you were sales hire #1-3. You've built sales infrastructure before, not just executed within it.

- Existing relationships with cybersecurity ecosystem partners (VARs, integrators, strategic alliances).

- Background in AI/ML-driven security, SIEM/SOAR, detection and response, or cloud security platforms.

- Experience presenting at industry conferences and building market presence.

Why Work at Artemis? 

Make a real world impact. Help empower cybersecurity teams around the world to keep people safe from the most advanced AI-powered cyber threats.

Be challenged to be better than ever before. Our team includes some of the smartest and most driven people in the world. We guarantee you will learn more in 1 year here than 10 years anywhere else.

Build the foundation. You're not joining an established sales machine - you're building it. Your success creates the blueprint. Your deals prove the category. Your feedback shapes the product.

Significant upside. As our founding Account Executive, you'll have equity and earning potential that reflects the value you're creating.

If you are passionate about building enterprise sales from the ground up and want to help companies defend against AI-powered adversaries, we'd love to hear from you.

We offer a competitive compensation of $320,000-$360,000 per year, and a top-of-market equity component. A variety of factors are considered when determining the compensation, including a candidate’s professional experience. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed.
