title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
description:
Your Mission

This is a company built for growth, not comfort. 

When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone. 

We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences. 

Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in. 

If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you. 

What You’ll Own:

- Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.

- Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.

- Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.

- Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.

- Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.

- Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.

- Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

- You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.

- Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.

- Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.

- Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.

- You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.

- You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

- Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.

- Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.

- Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.

- Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.

- Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.

- Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.

- Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.

- Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

- Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.

- Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.

- See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.

- Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.

- Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

title: Computer Vision & AI Engineer - Interceptor C‑UAS (m/f/d)
description:
About the role: 

At Quantum Systems, we are building highly autonomous interceptor systems that must perceive, decide, and act under extreme latency, motion, and environmental constraints.

We are looking for a Computer Vision & AI Engineer to drive the perception stack of our Counter-UAS interceptor platform. You will work on low-latency camera pipelines, small-object detection, object tracking, sensor fusion, visual odometry, precision landing, camera calibration, embedded inference, and data pipelines for training and validation.

This role is suited for someone with a strong academic or practical background in computer vision, AI, robotics, or perception systems. A Master’s degree is expected; a PhD is a strong plus. We are open to ambitious early-career candidates if they bring strong technical depth, practical implementation skills, and the ability to own complex perception problems.

Your Mission

You will develop the vision and AI pipeline that turns raw camera data into actionable perception outputs for autonomous flight. This includes low-latency detection and tracking, motion-aware vision, sensor fusion with inertial data, 3D direction-vector estimation, GPS-denied navigation, and precision landing support.

What is your Day to Day Mission: 

- Bring up, optimize, and maintain high-performance camera pipelines, including CSI camera interfaces, raw image access, buffering, synchronization, and latency reduction.

- Develop detection algorithms for small and difficult-to-see objects in moving and rotating camera images.

- Combine machine learning and classical computer vision approaches where appropriate.

- Fuse inertial data, motion information, and visual data to improve detection and tracking in moving image sequences.

- Build object tracking pipelines that can switch from initial detection to low-latency tracking once a target has been acquired.

- Optimize perception pipelines for embedded execution on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

- Work toward high frame-rate processing targets in the range of 100–300 FPS, where technically feasible.

- Use camera intrinsics and extrinsics to transform image-space detections into 3D direction vectors or other navigation-relevant outputs.

- Work on GPS-denied navigation concepts using visual odometry, including approaches with forward-facing camera views rather than only downward-looking cameras.

- Develop visual support for precision landing, including height estimation, velocity estimation, and motion-state estimation from limited camera perspectives.

- Build and maintain the data pipeline from onboard recordings to cloud storage, preprocessing, annotation, dataset generation, training, validation, and benchmarking.

- Work with annotation tools such as SuperAnnotate, CVAT, Label Studio, or comparable systems.

- Benchmark and evaluate different model and algorithm families, including approaches such as CenterNet, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, optical flow, feature tracking, object detection, and lightweight embedded models.

- Build deployment pipelines using ONNX, TensorRT, custom inference runners, or comparable embedded inference tooling.

- Collaborate closely with autonomy, flight control, embedded software, test, and systems engineering teams.

What you bring to the team: 

- Master’s degree or PhD in computer vision, AI, robotics, machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a comparable technical field.

- Strong understanding of computer vision fundamentals, camera geometry, feature detection, object detection, tracking, calibration, and image-space to 3D transformations.

- Practical experience implementing computer vision or machine learning pipelines in Python and C++ .

- Experience with embedded inference, ideally on NVIDIA Jetson , CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX, GStreamer, V4L2, or similar technologies.

- Ability to read, understand, and implement ideas from current research papers.

- Understanding of latency, throughput, profiling, memory movement, and real-time constraints.

- Experience with dataset creation, annotation workflows, training/validation splits, metrics, and benchmarking.

- Strong mathematical intuition and willingness to debug both algorithms and real-world sensor data.

- Ability to take ownership of a technical area and drive it from research prototype to flight-test-ready software.

- Experience with UAV perception, robotics perception, visual odometry, SLAM, sensor fusion, or tracking systems.

- Experience with IMU-camera fusion, ego-motion compensation, rolling-shutter effects, or high-frame-rate cameras.

- Experience with precision landing, visual navigation, or GPS-denied navigation.

- Experience building cloud-based ML training and validation pipelines.

- Publications, thesis work, GitHub projects, demos, or competition results in computer vision, robotics, AI, or autonomous systems.

title: Director of Deployment
description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role 

We're looking for a Director of Deployment to lead our Solutions team, the engineers who get our product live in industrial customers' plants, and to make every deployment faster, better and more reliable than the last.

You'll be accountable for every deployment we run, and be the senior escalation route, for our team and our customers, when something gets stuck.

This is a new role, and a leadership role, but a hands-on one. You'll coach our solutions engineers and leaders as they own deployments and customer relationships themselves, and step in yourself when a plant needs it. You'll work with Product, Machine Learning and Engineering to decide what goes back into the core product, so every plant is faster than the last.

What will this role achieve? 

The goal: Take Gigaton from 9 plants live to 50 by the end of 2027, with every new plant going from signed contract to the end of evaluation in 8 weeks.

Outcome – 50 plants live. You've taken us from 9 plants to 50 by 31 December 2027, across our customers worldwide. You've planned how many engineers we need and which teams new joiners go into, tracked the health of the whole portfolio every week, and stepped in early when a deployment started to drift.

Outcome – 8 weeks from contract to results. Today a plant takes about six months to reach evaluation. You've cut that to 8 weeks end to end, and published the numbers that prove it. title: Senior sustainability advisor (Engagement manager - Jr. partner level)
description:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

We are looking for an experienced sustainability professional to join our growing Sustainability Advisory team. The team serves as a strategic advisor to Watershed's customers , including more than 20% of the Fortune 500, helping them advance their corporate sustainability programs.

Our primary areas of focus include:

- Decarbonization planning and execution across Scopes 1-3

- Climate target setting, (e.g., SBTi-aligned targets)

- Voluntary and regulatory disclosures, (e.g., CSRD, UK SRS, CDP)

Beyond customer engagements, the Sustainability Advisory team serves as a trusted internal source of expertise. We partner with the Product team to bring sustainability intelligence into the Watershed platform, and with the Go-to-Market team to strengthen Watershed’s expertise, differentiation, and thought leadership.

In this role, you’ll be a highly trusted advisor to sustainability leaders at some of the world’s largest and most consequential companies. You’ll help shape sustainability strategies that make business sense, create the foundation for bold action, and advance progress on complex climate and environmental challenges. You’ll also help build the market-leading corporate sustainability platform by supporting teams across Watershed.

This role is intended for candidates with experience at the Senior Manager or Engagement Manager level, or above, at a leading consulting firm. The scope, autonomy, business acumen, and sustainability expertise required are comparable to those expected at that level or above.

You will 

- Advise sustainability leaders at many of the world’s leading companies on advancing their sustainability programs. You’ll independently lead strategic engagements across target setting, decarbonization, environmental impact management, and voluntary and regulatory reporting. Working closely with customers, you’ll develop practical strategies and build the business case for sustainability throughout their journey.

- Build sustainability intelligence by staying ahead of emerging frameworks, regulations, and market developments. You’ll translate the latest sustainability trends and regulatory changes into clear, actionable guidance for customers and internal teams, helping them remain compliant, competitive, and prepared for what’s next.

- Help develop new products and services by exploring emerging sustainability needs across topics and industries. You’ll prototype new ways to create value for customers and expand Watershed’s impact at the intersection of sustainability, advisory, and technology.

- Shape Watershed’s expertise and point of view by contributing to thought leadership, customer-facing materials, and internal enablement. You’ll help establish Watershed as a trusted partner for companies navigating the future of corporate sustainability.

What we’re looking for 

- 10+ years of professional experience, including at least 4 years at a consulting firm in client-facing roles and at least 4 years working in sustainability.

- Deep expertise in corporate decarbonization and familiarity with key climate frameworks, including the GHG Protocol, PCAF, SBTi, ISO standards, and relevant reporting frameworks and regulations such as CSRD, LSRS, CCDAA, ASRS, ISSB, and CDP.

- The ability to think clearly about complex problems and work confidently with data. You are systematic, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills. You can present complex analyses and recommendations to C-suite audiences and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- A track record of driving strategic initiatives in complex organizations. You can influence decision-making while managing multiple internal and external stakeholders across organizational levels.

- A strong interest in solving climate change and enthusiasm for helping define the future of corporate sustainability at a high-growth company.

Nice to have 

- Fluency in multiple languages, such as English, Spanish, French, or German.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) 

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations , lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

Own the strategy and the stack 

- Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.

- Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.

- Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.

- Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

- Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.

- Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.

- Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

- Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.

- Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical 

- Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.

- Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

- Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team 

- Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

- Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

- Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

Experience 

- Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

- Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

- Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft 

- Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

- Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

- Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

- Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

- Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. What You'll Do

- Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

- Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team 

- Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

- Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

- Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

- Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

- Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

- Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft 

- Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

- Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

- Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

- Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

- Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct 

- You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.

- You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.

- Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.

Why This Role 

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. title: Engineering Team Lead, Serverless Containers
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU.

On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own.

That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure.

What You Will Do

- Own the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero — across CPU and GPU.

- Make cold starts a solved problem: snapshotting, prewarming, image-layer caching, whatever it takes for scale-from-zero to feel instant.

- Treat AI workloads as the normal case: GPU-backed containers, streaming responses, long-lived connections, MCP servers that cost almost nothing while idle.

- Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

- Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

- Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

- Partner with Product Managers to turn platform decisions into a product developers want to deploy on.

What We're Looking For

- 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

- You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

- You have built container or workload platforms — orchestration, scheduling, isolation, request routing — not just deployed onto someone else's serverless platform.

- Deep Linux: namespaces, cgroups, image layers, page cache — comfortable well below the application layer.

- Multi-tenancy instincts: density, isolation, and fairness when hundreds of customers share one fleet.

- Significant experience building complex backend or infrastructure systems.

- You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

- A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

title: Conseiller(ère) commercial(e) terrain expérimenté(e)
description:
Indépendant | Rémunération à la commission uniquement | Territoire de vente local | Commissions déplafonnées

À propos de l'opportunité

Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l'aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants.

En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d'opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.

Vous devrez justifier d'une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.

Vos missions

- Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.

- Cibler les entreprises locales générant d'importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.

- Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.

- Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.

- Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.

- Établir des relations avec les chefs d'entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.

- Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d'optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.

- Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.

- Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.

Ce que nous recherchons

Indispensable

- Au moins un an d'expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l'énergie, les technologies d'entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l'approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.

- Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.

- Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.

- Des résultats démontrables en matière d'acquisition de nouveaux clients et d'atteinte d'objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu.

- La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections.

- Un bon sens de l'organisation et un suivi rigoureux.

- La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d'expérience et à persévérer.

- Une bonne compréhension du statut d'indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients.

- La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients.

Atouts

- Un réseau existant de chefs d'entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.

- Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente.

Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.

Rémunération

Il s'agit d'une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l'activité des commerçants apportés.

Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner :

- Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions.

- Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème.

- Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème.

- Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans.

- Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois.

- Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales.

Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d'activité du programme ; un barème Agent de 40 %, sans commissions résiduelles, peut s'appliquer.

Les conditions d'éligibilité, les bases de calcul et les modalités de versement sont précisées dans le contrat et présentées avant tout engagement. Les commissions s'entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables.

Formation et accompagnement

Nous vous aiderons à vous familiariser avec les produits et leur commercialisation grâce à un parcours initial et à un accompagnement continu couvrant la prospection, les entretiens de vente, les démonstrations, la gestion des objections et l'accompagnement des clients.

Les modalités du parcours initial et les prérequis à la commercialisation vous seront communiqués avant le démarrage.

Votre interlocuteur SumUp vous apportera également son soutien en matière de développement territorial, d'analyse de vos opportunités et de conseils commerciaux, dans le respect de votre autonomie d'organisation.

Commercial terrain, Commercial itinérant, Sales, Freelance, Vente, Commercial B2B, Commercial indépendant, Développement commercial. 

Job Application Tip 

We recognise that candidates feel they need to meet 100% of the job criteria in order to apply for a job. Please note that this is only a guide. If you don't tick every box, it's ok too because it means you have room to learn and develop your career at SumUp.

title: Sales Account Executive - Cybersecurity
description:
Passionate about Cybersecurity, open-source or network effect products? Interested in Sales? 

Join CrowdSec to build a safer internet for everyone.

What we do 

We aim to deter opportunistic and organized cybercrime through an Internet-scale, real-time security network. This network is powered by hundreds of thousands of servers sharing the aggression they block with our open-source software. By coupling this local behavior analysis and sharing its findings within our community, we create a real-time map of IP addresses used by cybercriminals, a large-scale reputation system, and a Crowd-Sourced Cyber Threat Intelligence of unprecedented magnitude that will counter the vast majority of technical hacks.

Who We Are 

CrowdSec is a human-sized team of cybersecurity experts. Most of the team has worked remotely since day 1. The CrowdSec solution is used in 180+ countries, it is a well-known, unique, collaborative, open-source security solution that protects hundreds thousands of users. We are animated by a mission: making the Internet a safer place, all together.

Role 

As an Account Executive (AE), you will work with the Sales team to help them scale, create new opportunities, interact with them, convert them to Leads, and take the accounts to signature. This will be done in collaboration with the BDRs, presales, Marketing, and Support teams to ensure the most pleasant customer journey.

Must-have 

- A track record of success in selling Cybersecurity software solutions

- Knowledges of fundamental cybersecurity mechanism

- The ability to build relationships and credibility with both SOC Managers/analysts, DevOps, SecOps, Risk Managers, and C-level Executives alike

- Predictability and accurate forecasting capabilities

- Fluency in English and at least a second language; any supplementary languages are considered a plus

Optional 

- You have sold to SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, MSSPs or MSPs

- Knowledge of the open-software landscape

- Languages other than English and French are considered a plus

- Start-up experience

- Experience with Hubspot

Soft Skills 

- You are a confident and polished communicator able to build strong and lasting relationships

- You are autonomous, do not hesitate to share new ideas with the team, and are genuinely interested in learning your customer's needs

- You are located in a +/- 6h from CEST Timezone

Why join CrowdSec? 

- You want to take part in an adventure with a bleeding edge tech startup

- Work with a team of blackbelt pros in their fields and interact with an exciting community

- You are driven and energetic, with a passion for prospecting and driving pipeline

- We are a full-remote company, we meet twice a year to strengthen the team spirit during a 1-week seminar.

title: Enterprise Account Executive - Financial Services
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We’re looking for an experienced, motivated Enterprise Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs’ growth across Financial Services: the banks, credit unions, insurers, lenders, and wealth managers people trust with their money, their families, and their futures. These institutions win or lose on trust and service at massive scale, under some of the most demanding regulatory standards anywhere. Their customers increasingly expect to talk, not type, whether they’re checking a balance, disputing a charge, filing a claim, or asking about a loan.

Our ideal candidate learns fast, closes well from a warm introduction, and is passionate about AI voice technology. You’ll act as a strategic partner to institutions reimagining how they serve, sell to, and sound to their customers, safely and at scale.

In this role you will: 

- Win net-new logos and drive ElevenAgents deal volume. These are the two metrics that define success in this role

- Be able to balance a diverse pipeline of large financial institutions who require white glove experience with medium sized regional clients who require speed to close

- Partner with the Enterprise Sales Lead to turn warm introductions into qualified opportunities and closed deals

- Identify where conversational AI can drive growth, automation, or cost efficiency in customer-facing and internal workflows. Our public use cases include account inquiries, payment support, fraud triage, loan origination, claims processing, collections, and compliance verification. Others include caller verification, onboarding, policy servicing and renewals, and contact center coaching

- Stay current on the conversational AI landscape, including competitive solutions, build-vs-buy dynamics, and emerging trends in AI governance and model risk

- Develop and execute account strategies across the whole buying group (CX and Contact Center Operations, Digital and Product, Technology, and Risk, Compliance, Legal, and InfoSec), landing with one high-impact use case and expanding across lines of business

- Partner closely with Forward Deployed Engineers to solution high-impact use cases, manage a successful Proof of Value, guide customers through model-risk, security, and architecture review, and set them up to scale in production

- Partner closely with Legal teams to drive strategic, fast-moving negotiations

- Serve as a trusted advisor on generative AI and voice, and share what you learn in the field to sharpen our Financial Services positioning, messaging, and references

Requirements 

- At least 7+ years of quota-carrying enterprise sales experience in SaaS or technology, ideally with exposure to AI, generative AI, LLM-based products, or API-driven platforms

- Financial services experience (banks, credit unions, insurers, lenders, payments) is preferred but not required. We weigh demonstrated adaptability and fast ramp in a new industry heavily

- Proven success closing [six- and seven-figure] deals and managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

- Proven ability to take a warm introduction through discovery, Proof of Value, and procurement to close

- Experience selling to both technical buyers (product and engineering) and business buyers (CX, operations, digital), and to risk and compliance gatekeepers, translating complex technology into business value

- Adept at deeply understanding a customer’s business and translating ElevenLabs’ capabilities into solutions that deliver against their needs

- Proficient in enterprise procurement, security review, and legal processes, including regulated-industry vendor risk, model risk, and data protection reviews, and able to work autonomously as a cross-functional partner

- Strong executive presence, the ability to build relationships with senior executives, and willingness to travel frequently for onsite client visits and conferences

- High EQ, self-aware, and curious. Low ego and hands-on, comfortable running your own prospecting and deals

- Comfort in an early-stage, high-growth environment, where ambiguity is the norm and the state of play changes rapidly

- Passion for voice and conversational AI and how it can unlock transformative value for customers

Location 
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in the United States, however the ability to operate in EST, CST, or PST timezones is required. There is a preference for candidates to be based in New York or San Francisco, with the option to work out of our office.

With HousingAnywhere, Kamernet, and Studapart under our roof, we’re Europe’s largest student rental platform. You’ll find us in Rotterdam, Paris, and Cergy, always guided by our four core values: Ownership, We are enablers, We are changemakers, and We are connectors.

To support our continued growth, we are creating a new, strategic role at the heart of operational performance and customer experience. There is no Quality & Training activity in the Group today : you will build it from the ground up.

Your role 

As Quality & Training Manager, you will create and lead the Quality & Training activity for the whole HousingAnywhere Group, covering the Operations teams in Cergy and Rotterdam. You define its scope, methods and tools, and you are responsible for service quality and operational practices across the Group.

You work closely with the managers of the Customer Support and Booking Ops teams to structure training, onboarding, quality monitoring and performance tooling.

The role is based in France, with frequent travel to our Rotterdam office. English is the main working language.

Building the Quality & Training activity 

- Design the Quality & Training activity : scope, operating model, priorities and roadmap,

- Set up the tools, rituals and governance needed to run the activity at Group level,

- Harmonise quality and training practices between the Cergy and Rotterdam teams,

- Lay the foundations for the activity to grow as needs evolve.

Training & onboarding 

- Identify the training needs of the Ops teams, and accompany the integration process while migrating to a single operating model in 2027,

- Develop complete training programmes covering customer service posture, tools, and day-to-day processes and procedures,

- Create and maintain training materials (scripts, practical guides, process sheets, e-learning content), working with the other departments like Product for new features,

- Run a structured onboarding and support new joiners in live situations after initial training, to bridge theory and practice,

- Carry out an individual assessment at the end of onboarding (audits, call listening, double listening, tests) and provide personalised follow-up,

- Lead group and one-to-one sessions, on-the-spot debriefs and targeted coaching on the fundamentals: call handling, request qualification, rephrasing, quality of written and spoken answers, and CRM data entry,

- Train teams on new procedures and tool changes as they are rolled out.

Quality & operational performance 

- Define and roll out quality standards and control frameworks for each team, across the full user journey,

- Build structured quality reporting by individual, team and business unit, with a monthly report to managers,

- Analyse interactions, indicators and recurring errors to identify root causes and drive continuous improvement plans,

Knowledge management 

- Collaborate with the Ops Project Manager to maintain the knowledge base,

- Build a culture of knowledge sharing and self-learning (e-learning) to reduce reliance on informal mentoring.

Cross-functional collaboration 

- Contribute to Voice of Customer and customer satisfaction projects by sharing pain points identified through quality monitoring,

- Propose initiatives to align operational practices with company strategy and the user experience.

- Advise and support managers on using tools and analysing performance.

Your profile 

- 5+ years of experience in training, quality management or quality monitoring of customer service or operations teams.

- Experience building a quality or training activity from scratch, or a strong drive to do so,

- Experience setting up a quality monitoring programme (call listening, audits, calibration),

- Solid knowledge of customer service best practices and operational process management,

- Ability to analyse spoken and written interactions and turn them into concrete recommendations,

- Teaching skills, structure and a results focus, with the ability to convince and motivate teams,

- Comfortable with CRM and telephony tools, e-learning content creation and performance dashboards,

- Fluent English and French are required. English is the main working language,

- Willingness to travel frequently to Rotterdam.

Why this opportunity? 

- A newly created role: you build the Group's Quality & Training activity from the ground up.

- Group-wide impact across our teams in Cergy and Rotterdam.

- A high level of autonomy to design tools, processes and training materials.

- An international environment, working between France and the Netherlands.

- A role combining training, quality and operations, both strategic and hands-on.

What’s in it for you 

- Position based in our Cergy office.

- Executive status with 218 workdays/year (with RTT days off).

- 50% transport costs covered.

- 70% health insurance coverage.

- Meal vouchers.

- Contribution to fitness membership costs.

- Christmas gift vouchers.

- Team-building events and much more!

title: Head of Legal - Financial Services
description:
🧡 About Alma 

At Alma, we believe sustainable commerce depends on fair, well‑balanced trade. Because finance plays a pivotal role in business, our mission is to put it back in its rightful place - serving merchants and consumers.

Our installment and deferred payment solutions help merchants boost sales by 20% or more, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless shopping experience - without encouraging bad debt.

As the buy now pay later leader in France and active in 10 European countries, we've empowered over +25,000 merchants and 10 million consumers.

With 400+ Almakers and €100M+ ARR, Alma is scaling rapidly across Europe as a member of the Next40, and we're just getting started!

👐 About the team 

The Head of Legal supports Alma to grow safely and sustainably by anticipating and managing legal risk, providing pragmatic advice, negotiating contracts, and supporting teams across the company; in a strongly regulated environment.

The Head of Legal reports to Alma’s General Secretary and lead the Legal function. You will be a trusted partner to the Director’s Committee and work closely with Product, Tech, Sales, Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Information Security and People.

You will also act as Alma’s Data Protection Officer, with the independence, resources and direct access to senior management required to perform the role effectively.

This is a permanent position based in Paris.

💼 About the job 

As Head of Legal, you will define Alma’s legal and privacy strategy and ensure that it supports the company’s business ambitions, regulatory obligations and risk appetite.

Your main responsibilities will include:

Define and lead Alma’s legal strategy 

- Develop and execute a clear legal roadmap aligned with Alma’s business and international strategy.

- Identify, assess and manage Alma’s main legal risks, escalating material matters to executive management and governance bodies when appropriate.

- Provide clear, pragmatic and business-oriented advice to the Executive Committee and teams across Alma.

- Translate complex legal requirements into actionable recommendations, policies and scalable operational processes.

- Monitor relevant legal developments across Alma’s markets and anticipate their impact on the company’s products and activities.

Support Alma’s business, products and partnerships 

- Advise Product and Tech teams throughout the design and launch of new products and features, embedding legal and privacy considerations from the outset.

- Support Sales, Account Management, Operations and other business teams on strategic projects and complex legal questions.

- Oversee the drafting, review and negotiation of commercial agreements, including agreements with merchants, partners, suppliers and technology providers.

- Establish scalable contracting standards, templates, playbooks and approval processes that enable teams to move quickly while controlling legal risk.

- Advise on strategic transactions, partnerships, outsourcing arrangements and international expansion projects.

Oversee corporate and governance matters 

- Manage Alma’s corporate legal matters and ensure that its legal entities comply with applicable governance and corporate requirements.

- Support executive management and governance bodies in preparing decisions and maintaining appropriate corporate documentation.

- Advise on financing, corporate transactions, intellectual property, competition law and other strategic legal matters.

- Coordinate external counsel and manage the legal budget, ensuring that external expertise is used effectively.

- Oversee litigation, pre-litigation, claims and other disputes, defining the appropriate strategy and protecting Alma’s interests.

Act as Alma’s Data Protection Officer 

- Define and oversee Alma’s data protection framework in accordance with the GDPR and other applicable privacy laws.

- Inform and advise Alma and its employees on their data protection obligations.

- Monitor compliance through appropriate policies, processes, controls and reporting.

- Maintain and continuously improve Alma’s privacy governance, including records of processing activities, privacy notices, retention standards and procedures for handling data-subject requests.

- Establish a robust framework for data protection impact assessments and ensure that DPIAs are conducted when required.

- Advise Product, Tech, Data, Risk, Operations, Marketing and People teams on privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default principles.

- Work closely with Information Security on personal-data breaches, incident response, security measures and regulatory notifications.

- Act as Alma’s primary contact for data protection authorities and cooperate with them when required.

- Develop training and awareness initiatives to foster a strong data protection culture throughout Alma.

Lead and develop the Legal team 

- Set a clear vision, priorities and operating model for the Legal team.

- Manage, coach and develop team members, promoting high standards of expertise, ownership and collaboration.

- Allocate resources according to business priorities and ensure that legal requests are handled effectively.

- Define meaningful objectives and indicators to measure the team’s impact, service quality and risk management.

- Build trusted relationships across Alma and position Legal as both a strategic partner and an independent control function.

🧩 About you 

You combine excellent legal judgment with a strong understanding of business. You are comfortable taking clear positions on complex matters while remaining pragmatic and solution-oriented.

You are likely to thrive in this role if you:

- Can move comfortably between strategic questions and hands-on legal work.

- Understand how to balance business velocity, customer experience, innovation and legal risk.

- Communicate complex legal matters clearly to both legal and non-legal audiences.

- Build trusted relationships with senior leaders and challenge decisions constructively when necessary.

- Enjoy developing people and creating clarity for a multidisciplinary team.

- Are comfortable working with incomplete information and taking ownership of sensitive or high-impact decisions.

- Have strong negotiation, drafting and stakeholder-management skills.

- Are fluent in both French and English.

Your experience

- You hold a Master’s degree in law or an equivalent legal qualification.

- You have significant experience in senior legal positions (15+ years), combining experience in a leading bank or FinTech and a law firm.

- You have strong expertise in banking, commercial and technology contracts, corporate matters and business law.

- Experience supporting international activities and working across several European jurisdictions would also be valuable.

- You have the level of expertise and professional standing required to act as Data Protection Officer.

description:

👐 About the team

Alma is a lender. We originate several million consumer receivables a year, carry them for a few weeks, and refinance them off a deliberately light balance sheet through securitization vehicles (Fonds Communs de Titrisation) and our other funding lines. We are regulated as a société de financement and a payment institution.

That changes what "accounting" means here. A lender's accounts are not a monthly deliverable produced at the end of a chain: they are the chain . Every payment event, every commission, every provision, every sale of receivables to an FCT has to become a journal entry that ties — to the transaction underneath it, to the general ledger above it, and to the prudential statements the regulator reads. At our scale and growth, this is a strategic topic, and one that is as much about data as it is about accounting.

Today the chain exists: an internal core banking ledger we built ourselves, feeding NetSuite, feeding regulatory reporting. What it does not have is a single owner who understands it end-to-end, holds it to the standard a regulated lender needs, and evolves it as the business changes (geographies, products, licenses). That is the role we are opening.

You will join an Accounting team inside a Finance organization of ~15 people covering Strategic Financing, FP&A, Accounting, Regulatory reporting and Controlling. You will report to the Head of Financing & Accounting, alongside the Financing team and the General Accounting Manager, who oversees corporate cycles, tax, statutory and consolidated accounts.

This is a role with unusual ownership for its level: the banking accounting scope is yours from day one, and so is the data chain that produces it.

💼 About the job

Own the accounting of the credit business: 

- Own how the portfolio is represented in the books: origination, revenue recognition on merchant and customer commissions, deferred income, write-offs and recoveries, cost of risk and provisioning on performing and non-performing exposures.

- Own the accounting of our securitizations: sales of receivables to the FCTs, derecognition, discount and over-collateralisation, residual interests, servicing and management fees, hedging.

- Own the accounting of our funding: corporate debt, commercial paper, and the new funding instruments we add as the refinancing strategy evolves.

Own the core banking ledger: 

- Be the functional owner of the engine that turns business events into accounting: which event, which account, which currency, which date, which counterparty.

- Specify and validate the accounting schemes for every new product, partner and geography, and work with Engineering and Data on the ledger's model, its feed into the ERP, and the fixes when something drifts.

- Own the audit trail end-to-end — from a single €40 installment to a line in a prudential statement — and make it documented enough to be walked through by someone whose job is to challenge it.

Reinforce the control framework: 

- Design and automate the reconciliations that hold the whole thing together: ledger ↔ general ledger ↔ bank ↔ FCT reporting ↔ prudential statements.

- Shorten monthly close, incl. turning a manual, end-of-month, spreadsheet-based check into an automated, evidenced, repeatable control.

- Be Finance's counterpart to Internal Control and Periodic Control on everything accounting-data related.

Own regulatory reporting: 

- Own the production and the quality of our prudential and statistical reporting — solvency, large exposures, liquidity, and the statistical returns that go with them.

- Own the reconciliation tables that matter most: prudential statements to accounting balances, regulatory returns to the trial balance, own funds and RWA back to their audit trail.

- Own the reporting tooling and its data feeds, and work with the Regulatory and Financing teams on the evolutions of the prudential framework and on the treatment of our securitizations.

🧩 About you

To succeed in this job: 

- You have around 6-7 years of experience, ideally starting in audit of financial services — banks, consumer credit, asset management, securitization — in a Big 4 or a specialised practice, possibly with a first move in-house. You know how to build a number, prove it, and defend it line by line in front of people whose job is to challenge it.

- You know banking accounting for real: French banking GAAP, the PCEC, cost of risk, revenue recognition on credit products. Or you know financial services accounting well enough that the banking layer is a matter of months, not years.

- You actually enjoy controls at scale — reconciling large populations, hunting the anomaly, chasing the last twelve euros of a four-hundred-million balance until you know exactly where they went. If that sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this is not your role.

- You are autonomous and scrappy. On things to build, or on things that already exist.

- You are fluent in English and French — our documentation and our regulator are French, part of our business and our team are not.

And it will be nice if you also: 

- Hold, or are working towards, the DEC (or CPA, ACCA, equivalent).

- Have been exposed to securitization — FCTs, SPVs, waterfalls, deconsolidation — or to a regulated credit institution from the inside.

- You are autonomous on data. SQL is a daily tool, a data warehouse does not intimidate you, and your reflex in front of a five-million-row population is to query it, not to ask someone for a summary. This is the single most important line in this job description.

- Know NetSuite, BigQuery, dbt or Python.

title: Lead Fraud & AML Ops
description:
Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière.

Notre vision 

Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes.

Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise.

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

À propos de Pennylane 

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1200 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours 

🚀 Déjà plus de 1 500,000 TPE/PME et plus de 7000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Role context

Pennylane currently operates around 50,000 business accounts through a BaaS model with Swan and is applying for Établissement de paiement and Société de financement licences. As we prepare to onboard new customers under our own licensed entity from mid-2027, we are building our first line of defence across onboarding, transaction monitoring, fraud and risk operations.

As Transaction Monitoring & Fraud Operations Lead , you will be one of the first operational leaders in this greenfield setup. Reporting to the Head of FinCrime Operations, you will lead first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations across Pennylane’s payment activities within a single team. You will own first-line alert handling and fraud case management, with clear escalation paths to Compliance and Risk.

Your mission will be to build and launch Pennylane’s first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations, then scale the team and its workflows as volumes grow—while maintaining strong decision quality, auditability and customer protection.

This is a high-autonomy role with direct exposure to a strategic regulatory project and close collaboration with Product, Compliance and Risk. You will help shape how Pennylane protects the financial activity of French SMEs as it brings more of its regulated operations in-house.

Responsibilities

- Own end-to-end first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for business customers, ensuring that alert triage, investigations, customer outreach and escalations are completed in line with policies set by Compliance and Risk and within agreed SLAs.

- Translate AML/CFT and fraud policies into operational procedures, decision trees and analyst playbooks, and provide evidence-based recommendations on alert quality and operational bottlenecks.

- Review complex or high-risk alerts within the first-line mandate, oversee post-onboarding fraud cases and ensure that escalations, customer complaints and law-enforcement requests are handled with complete, auditable records.

- Implement the QA and reporting framework, monitor operational and risk indicators, and support Compliance during controls testing, audits and regulatory reviews.

- Recruit, onboard and lead the transaction monitoring and fraud analyst team, combining hands-on support with effective coaching and a culture of rigour, accountability and continuous learning.

- Establish the team’s performance and capacity framework, covering SLAs, productivity, quality, backlogs, false-positive rates and hiring needs.

- Partner with Product and Tech to test and improve transaction-monitoring, fraud and back-office workflows, prioritising automation while identifying the controls and decisions that should remain manual.

First 6–12 months

- Deliver approved operating procedures, analyst playbooks and escalation rules before go-live.

- Establish a capacity and hiring plan based on observed alert volumes and handling times.

- Validate that alert queues, evidence collection, account measures and second-line handovers work operationally before launch.

- By go-live, have first-line monitoring operational for new customers, with trained coverage, agreed SLAs, documented QA controls and named escalation owners.

What we’re looking for

- Significant experience in transaction monitoring, fraud or broader financial-crime operations within a regulated financial-services environment, including ownership of operational performance and complex case decisions.

- Proven experience leading and developing an operational team responsible for alert queues or investigations, combining effective coaching with a hands-on player-coach approach when needed.

- Strong understanding of first-line alert handling: triage, investigation, typology, escalation, and the difference between a fraud case and an AML case.

- Good working knowledge of French and European AML/CFT expectations, including ACPR and TRACFIN requirements, and experience translating policy into SOPs, decision trees and analyst guidance.

- Experience working with Product or Tech on workflow or tooling changes.

- Sound judgement on what to automate, what to sample and what to escalate.

- Ability to use operational metrics to manage quality, backlogs and capacity.

- Ability to make structured, well-documented decisions under pressure and communicate complex cases clearly to operational and compliance stakeholders.

- Comfort building operations in a greenfield environment where volumes are still uncertain and tooling is evolving.

- Exposure to ACPR expectations, a licensing programme, a BaaS migration or law-enforcement requests would be an advantage.

Languages, presence and location

- Fluent French and English are mandatory.

- Based in France, with a strong preference for Paris.

- Regular on-site presence in Paris is expected. Partial remote is possible. This is not a fully remote role.

Why join

- Build first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for a new regulated entity from the ground up.

- Shape the operating model before launch, rather than inheriting fixed processes and tooling.

- Take ownership of a critical domain with a direct impact on go-live readiness, customer protection and responsible growth.

- Work closely with Operations, Compliance, Risk, Product and Tech on a strategic company project.

Recruitment Process

1. Interview with Lucie (30-45 min), Senior Recruiter

2. Interview with Maxime (1h), General Manager

3. Case Study with Laurent and Léa (1h)

4. Last round with Stanislas and Felix (45 min)

Candidature uniquement via nos canaux officiels : postulez exclusivement via nos offres publiées sur nos supports officiels (site carrière, pages officielles partenaires).

Nous ne vous demanderons jamais de paiement, ni d’informations financières (coordonnées bancaires, paiement pour un entretien, achat de matériel, etc.) dans le cadre du recrutement. 

Si une telle demande vous est faite, il s’agit d’une fraude. Nous vous invitons à ne pas répondre et à nous le signaler immédiatement ." 

Encourageant la diversité, équité et inclusion sous toutes ses formes, Pennylane offre un environnement de travail inclusif, bienveillant et propice à l’épanouissement, dans nos bureaux et en remote. Nous nous engageons à fournir les mêmes chances à tous nos candidats, indépendamment de leurs origines sociales et ethniques, genres, religions, orientations sexuelles ou handicaps. 

🇫🇷 Données personnelles 

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. Pennylane processes your data to manage your application and assess your suitability for the position. If your application is unsuccessful, your data may be retained for 2 years from our last exchange or the closing of the recruitment process, in order to build and manage a candidate pool. Your focus will be on applying the credit policy, running controls and turning that policy into day-to-day operations, in close collaboration with our Product and Business teams.

As Credit Operations Lead , you will build and launch the first-line credit operations function for Pennylane’s own-book financing activity. Reporting to the Managing Director, you will translate Risk’s credit policy into executable decisions, controlled workflows and auditable outcomes.

You will initially remain hands-on across origination, manual reviews, exception handling and portfolio monitoring. As volumes grow, you will scale the operating model, tooling and team in close collaboration with Risk, Product and our financing partner.

This is a high-autonomy, greenfield role at the heart of Pennylane’s future licensed operations.

Responsibilities

- Own the end-to-end execution of credit origination, including manual reviews, decisions within the delegated first-line mandate, exception handling and escalation to Risk. Ensure that outcomes meet agreed SLAs and are supported by a complete audit trail.

- Build the credit operating model, including procedures, decision trees, delegated authorities, first-line controls, operational KPIs and escalation paths.

- Own first-line operational monitoring of the active book, including repayment incidents, early-warning signals and the follow-up actions required by the credit policy.

- Build the operational relationship with the financing partner, with clear responsibilities, service levels and escalation processes for servicing, disbursement and collection incidents.

- Provide Risk with structured feedback on policy effectiveness, operational impact and emerging portfolio signals. Risk remains accountable for risk appetite, policy approval and independent oversight.

- Partner with Product, Tech, Risk and Data to design origination workflows, analyst tools and scoring processes, translate operational needs into product requirements, and determine what to automate or retain for human review.

- Remain hands-on during the launch phase, then recruit and lead the first credit analysts as volumes grow, establishing clear quality standards and a culture of rigour, accountability and customer clarity.

First 6–12 months

- Before the first own-book exposure, deliver an approved end-to-end operating model covering procedures, decision trees, delegated authorities, evidence requirements and escalation paths to Risk.

- Ensure that the origination workflow is operationally ready for launch by testing the main decision paths and failure scenarios with Product and Tech.

- Establish the initial management framework, including SLAs, quality controls, operational KPIs, portfolio-monitoring indicators and reporting to the second-line Risk function.

- Ensure that every credit decision can be reconstructed from the underlying data, evidence, applicable policy and recorded approvals.

- Define the initial capacity model, team coverage and hiring plan based on expected volumes, handling times and observed performance.

- By go-live, have trained operational coverage, named escalation owners and documented procedures for manual reviews, exceptions and partner incidents.

What we’re looking for

- Significant experience in credit or underwriting operations within a regulated financial-services environment, including manual reviews, delegated decisions, exceptions and audit trails.

- Experience managing operational quality, SLAs and capacity, with direct team leadership or a strong player-coach track record.

- Strong understanding of first-line credit operations and the respective responsibilities of Operations and Risk.

- Experience collaborating with Product or Tech teams on workflows, tooling and automation.

- Ability to use operational and portfolio indicators to identify early-warning signals, manage performance and plan capacity.

- Sound judgement on what to automate, what requires human review and when a case should be escalated.

- Ability to make structured, well-documented decisions and communicate them clearly to customers, partners and internal stakeholders.

- Experience with SME financing products, such as invoice financing or short-term working-capital facilities, would be a strong advantage.

Languages, presence and location

- Fluent French and English are mandatory.

- Based in France, with a strong preference for Paris.

- Regular on-site presence in Paris is expected. Partial remote is possible. This is not a fully remote role.

Why join

- Build the first-line credit operations function for Pennylane’s future société de financement from the ground up.

- Shape the operating model, tooling and team before the own-book financing activity reaches scale.

- Take ownership of a critical function with a direct impact on go-live readiness, customer experience and responsible growth.
