title: Daimler Buses – Automobil-Mechatroniker / Automobil-Fachmann (m/w) für Nutzfahrzeuge – Domdidier (Fribourg)
description:
Über unseren Mandanten Daimler Buses ist ein Tochterunternehmen der Daimler Truck AG und gehört zu den weltweit führenden Busherstellern. Mit den Marken Mercedes-Benz, Setra, OMNIplus und BusStore verkauft das Unternehmen nicht nur Busse, sondern bietet auch den kompletten Rundum-Service entlang der Wertschöpfungskette in der Schweiz. Mit durchdachten, nachhaltigen Mobilitätslösungen und einem breit gefächerten Service als Full-Line-Anbieter erfüllt es nahezu alle Bedürfnisse seiner Kunden im Bussegment.

Deine Aufgaben Suchst Du eine abwechslungsreiche Aufgabe, bei der Du mit Deinem technischen Können dafür sorgst, dass Reise- und Linienbusse zuverlässig unterwegs sind? 

Dann könnte diese Stelle zu Dir passen! Per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung sucht Daimler Buses für die Werkstatt in Domdidier (Friboug) einen Automobil-Mechatroniker / Automobil-Fachmann in Festanstellung.

Du hast Erfahrung aus dem Automobilbereich, aber bisher noch nicht mit Bussen gearbeitet? Das ist kein Problem: Für Daimler Buses zählen vor allem die richtige Einstellung und die Bereitschaft, Dich rasch in neue Themen einzuarbeiten.
Bei dieser Stelle übernimmst Du folgende Tätigkeiten: - Durchführen von Wartungs-, Reparatur- und Revisionsarbeiten an den von Daimler Buses betreuten Reise- und Linienbussen.
- Diagnostizieren von Störungen sowie Prüfen und Instandsetzen mechanischer Fahrzeugkomponenten und elektronischer Systeme.
- Aufbereiten von Neufahrzeugen.
- Dokumentieren der ausgeführten Arbeiten.
- Gelegentliche Übernahme des 24-Stunden-Bereitschaftsdienstes; dieser wird selbstverständlich zusätzlich vergütet.

Dein Profil - Abgeschlossene Berufsausbildung im Automobilbereich, zum Beispiel als Automobil-Mechatroniker EFZ oder Automobil-Fachmann EFZ. Eine Ausrichtung auf Nutzfahrzeuge ist von Vorteil, aber keine Voraussetzung.
- Idealerweise einige Jahre Berufserfahrung; Erfahrung mit Bussen ist nicht zwingend erforderlich.
- Gute Kenntnisse in Deutsch oder Französisch. Kenntnisse der jeweils anderen Sprache sind willkommen, aber keine Voraussetzung.
- Selbstständige, belastbare und flexible Arbeitsweise sowie eine offene und teamorientierte Persönlichkeit.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:

Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories — the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed. 

Every part we make generates data, decisions, and handoffs. Your job is to capture that knowledge, automate the work around it, and remove whatever slows production down. When a critical defense program needs parts by next week, the systems you build are why we can deliver. 

The Role As a Full-Stack Software Engineer on our manufacturing intelligence team, you'll work wherever the leverage is highest. One week that means turning an operator's spreadsheet into a proper workflow; the next it means wiring machine data into scheduling, or cutting a manual quoting step out of the order flow. 

You'll own problems end to end across our customer portal, Enterprise Resource Planning / Manufacturing Execution System, and the data layer connecting them to the shop floor. 

Based at our HQ at “The Circle” (Zurich airport), your work will span: 

- Manufacturing Intelligence: Capturing process, machine, and quality data so knowledge lives in systems instead of in people's heads. 

- Automation: Replacing manual steps in quoting, planning, scheduling, and documentation with software that runs on its own. 

- Production Acceleration: Finding the bottlenecks between CAD/CAM data submission and shipped parts. 

- Tools for People: Building interfaces that make life easier for operators, engineers, and customers, whether that's a work instruction screen, a dashboard, or a self-service portal. 

Importantly, you do not need prior experience in the manufacturing domain. We value a high level of curiosity and autonomy to find and solve problems. 

What We're Looking For - Experience: 3+ years as a software engineer with proven experience in shipping code to production, across backend and frontend 

- Broad Technical Range: Experience in systems design, architecture and implementation. In general, you don’t shy away from new technologies and pick up whatever the problem requires. Our current tech stack is: Rust, PostgreSQL, React, Python, AWS. 

- End-to-End Ownership: From talking to the user, to schema, to API, to UI, to rollout. You don't hand off "the other half." 

- Industrial Grit: Comfortable spending time on the shop floor in Germany to understand how work actually happens and how your software interacts with precision machinery. 

- Autonomy: You are comfortable with diving into new topics, coming up with solutions and driving their implementation 

- Bonus points: Knowledge of manufacturing and how factories operate, basic understanding of the Manufacturing Automation Pyramid 

- On-site: Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland. 

What we're not looking for - Engineers who only work on frontend or only work on backend. You must be comfortable across the full stack. 

- People who need detailed specs before they start building. You'll work directly with users and define the solution yourself. 

- Developers who ship code and move on. You own the outcome — not just the PR. 

- E ngineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities. 

What we offer - Mission: Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of Europe . Your work directly enables the production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space 

- Total Ownership: High-stakes autonomy in your domain. You own both the problems and the solutions, and have the authority to execute. 

- The Environment: You are building solutions to accelerate production in a 5,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial plastic and metal 3D printers. Your work affects production of physical parts from day one. 

- The Team: Growing team of experienced software engineers, who value an open feedback culture. You may (and are expected to) challenge the status quo, prior decisions and drive SAEKI’s way forward. 

- Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity. 

- Location: Zurich HQ with occasional travel to Factory ONE in Munich, Germany 

Apply - Resume: Focus on systems you've built and owned.

Working as a core member of the division production leadership team, you will lead a team of planner and warehouse specialists driving standardization and best practices. - Own and monitor key SIOP and Supply Chain KPIs: On Time Delivery (OTD), capacity utilization, inventory turns, and lead times.

Team Leadership

- Lead and develop a distributed team of demand planning and warehouse/stock specialists, setting clear goals while fostering a culture of data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement (Lean/Six Sigma mindset).

- Establish common ways of working, tools, and standards across sites to unify the supply chain function at division level.

MRP / ERP Management

- Act as subject matter expert for the MRP/ERP system regarding demand planning capabilities, and drive improvements to configuration, workflows, and data quality.

- Partner with IT/business systems teams on ERP upgrades, patches, and enhancements affecting planning modules across all sites; lead UAT (user acceptance testing) for planning-related system changes.

Finance Reporting

- Prepare and deliver a monthly production and delivery forecast to Finance to support anticipation of next month's revenues.

- Partner with Finance on monthly sales forecasts (revenue and volume implications), budget and variance analysis (actual vs. forecast/budget) at division level. 

- Plan and coordinate the annual physical inventory count at each site ensuring accuracy and working with Finance to reconcile results against ERP records.

Requirements: 

- Master’s degree in industrial engineering, Supply Chain Management, or related field required;

- 8+ years of progressive supply chain experience focused on demand/supply planning in a manufacturing environment. Experience in the electronics industry preferred.

- Experience operating across multiple sites and ability to standardize processes and drive alignment across locations 

- 3+ years of experience in leading a team

- Strong analytical and statistical data handling skills; advanced Excel required.

- Deep, hands-on expertise in MRP/ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics) is required

- Solid knowledge of finance/costing concepts (standard costing, inventory valuation, working capital, etc)

- Fluent in French and English (written and spoken) required, given the international, cross-functional nature of the role

- Structured problem-solving and data-driven decision-making

- Cross functional influence and clear communication to Senior Leadership and Finance Stakeholders.

title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description:
Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.

Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.

Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

title: Legal AI Counsel (Zurich)

When you join Legartis, you don't just take a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and legal experts. We don't chase hype; we build substance.

Your mission This is not a classic legal role, and not a classic sales or product role. You operate at the intersection of Law, Revenue, and AI, where you are a lever, not a bottleneck: your job is to build the demos, playbooks, and standards that let the whole company scale, and to step into the calls where your expertise closes the gap.

1. Commercial impact. You help win and grow customers. You build and run demos that create a "wow" moment, join high-stakes prospect calls as the legal expert who speaks at eye level with GCs, and run our trials and workshops: onboarding sessions where customers solve their own use cases live, with you coaching. You turn objections into use cases and interest into next steps, and you enable our Sales team to tell the legal story without you in the room. You think of outcomes in terms of trial-to-signature conversion, adoption, expansion.

2. Customer transformation. Once a deal is signed, you make the value real by acting as a strategic sparring partner in onboarding: defining review requirements, tuning playbooks and prompts, and showing legal teams where Legartis delivers the highest ROI. You turn individual learnings into scalable standards and documentation.

3. Making the AI better. You work hands-on with the Legal Agent: prompting, testing, diagnosing where it breaks and why. You feed what you learn from customers back into Product and Engineering (playbook quality, test sets, edge cases) so the product improves with every customer.

4. Internal legal support. You don't just sell the tool; you use it. When necessary, you support Legartis as in-house counsel on contract reviews and specific legal questions.

Your profile We are honest: people who combine all of this are rare. We hire for aptitude and attitude, assess hands-on in a case study, and train the rest side by side, in real customer work.

1. You can sell the product (key). Not in the cold-calling sense, but in the way a great expert sells: by making the customer succeed in front of their own team. Concretely, this means you can (or want to learn to):

- Run a live demo with confidence including customized, high-stakes demos and recover gracefully when something doesn't land: pull out a better prompt, adjust on the spot, turn a skeptical question into a stronger result.
- Coach the customer hands-on. In trials and hackathons, the customer drives and you navigate: you get them to enter their own real legal questions, create the first "wow" moment themselves, and build the habits (saved prompts, reusable workflows) that make them stay.
- Turn objections into use cases. When a customer says "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves," you respond with a concrete path: a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative. You're straight about limits, because credibility is what closes.

Staatsexamen is welcome but not required : we explicitly encourage candidates with qualifications from other jurisdictions or non-traditional paths (e.g. law + IT).

title: Value Strategist
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

This is a senior individual contributor role within our global Revenue organization, spanning the full customer lifecycle from early sales conversations through proof of concept, deployment, renewal, and expansion. You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

In this role you will 

- Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

- Build our global value strategy. Develop the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, discovery approaches, and playbooks that define how ElevenLabs approaches value across industries and use cases.

- Scale what works. Turn bespoke work with our largest customers into repeatable approaches that enable our Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial teams to articulate and measure value without requiring bespoke support for every customer.

- Identify where ElevenLabs can have the greatest impact. Develop a deep understanding of a customer's business, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities to determine which use cases have the greatest potential and why.

- Quantify the opportunity. Build rigorous financial and operational models that translate ElevenLabs use cases into measurable outcomes across revenue, cost, productivity, customer experience, and other relevant dimensions.

- Define how value will be proven. Establish success metrics and measurement approaches for proofs of concept and deployments so that customers and ElevenLabs have a shared understanding of what success looks like from the outset.

- Measure value realization. Partner with customers and internal teams after deployment to understand the impact ElevenLabs is delivering, identify gaps between expected and realized value, and determine where additional opportunities exist.

- Support expansion and long-term customer value. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.

- Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.

- Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.

- Influence senior stakeholders. Communicate complex analysis simply and credibly, and engage with senior leaders internally and externally when the opportunity requires it.

Requirements 

- 10+ years of relevant experience across operating roles, strategy, management consulting, analytics, finance, customer strategy, or other roles requiring rigorous business problem solving.

- Strong operating judgment. You understand how businesses work and can quickly get underneath a customer's operating model, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities.

- Exceptional analytical ability. You can personally build sophisticated financial and operational models, work with incomplete or imperfect information, make assumptions explicit, and turn analysis into decisions.

- Structured problem solving. You are comfortable starting with an ambiguous question such as "Where could AI create the most value in this business?" and developing a rigorous approach to answering it.

- Customer credibility. You can work directly with customers across functions and levels, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and establish trust quickly.

- Commercial judgment. You understand how business value connects to technology investment decisions and can partner closely with Revenue teams while maintaining an objective, customer-first perspective.

- Excellent communication. You can distill complex analysis into a clear point of view and communicate it effectively in writing and verbally, from working teams through senior executives.

- A builder mentality. You are excited to start by doing the work yourself, learn from customers, and turn what works into scalable methodologies and tools.

- Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You can move quickly across industries, customer types, and use cases while maintaining a high bar for analytical rigor.

- Ability to operate globally. You are comfortable partnering with teams and customers across regions and traveling when valuable for customer work.

- Willingness to travel. Must be willing and able to travel up to 10% of the time.

Bonus points 

- Experience in strategy or management consulting, particularly in operational transformation, technology, customer experience, or growth.

- Experience as an operator within a technology company or other fast-moving business.

- Experience working on AI, automation, customer experience, or technology-enabled business transformation.

- Experience developing business cases, value frameworks, or analytical methodologies that were ultimately scaled beyond an individual project or customer.

- Experience working with enterprise customers on complex, cross-functional initiatives.

Location 

This is a global role within the Revenue organization. The role can be based in San Francisco or remotely, with the option to work from our San Francisco office.

You will work with customers and ElevenLabs teams across regions and should expect travel for customer meetings and onsite work when it meaningfully advances the work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Senior Director, Market Access Strategy, International
description:
Mavericks Wanted 

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on 
  
In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.  
  
Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work. 

About BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. 

BridgeBio is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing, and delivering transformative medicines for patients living with genetic diseases and genetically defined cancers. Since our founding in 2015, we have built a diverse portfolio of more than 20 drug development programs, ranging from early discovery to late-stage clinical trials, across multiple therapeutic areas including precision oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, neurology, and renal disease. We have already achieved regulatory approval for three therapies and continue to advance promising science from academia into meaningful treatments for patients worldwide. 

Who We Are 

BridgeBio is a global biotechnology company with our Global Headquarters located in San Francisco, USA, and our International HQ located in Zug, Switzerland. Since establishing our European presence in 2021, we’ve been building empowered, high-performing teams across countries — with experienced colleagues who move quickly, take ownership, and are fueling the company’s international growth. 

At BridgeBio, you’ll find an energetic and collaborative culture where pragmatism meets bold decision-making. We embrace uncertainty with confidence, guided by our commitment to making a meaningful impact for patients. Our people are trusted and empowered, united by urgency, purpose, and the drive to advance science for patients around the world. 

To learn more about our story and company culture, visit us at https://bridgebio.com 

What You’ll Do

title: Technical Project Manager (Efector Development)
description:
As Destinus scales its vehicle programmes, we are looking for a dedicated Technical Project Manager to own execution across the full vehicle development stack – from propulsion and structures through avionics integration, ground support equipment, and qualification. This frees our engineers to focus on technical depth and our team leads on strategic leadership.

As one of the first hires in this group, you will manage a programme and help build the PM structure itself alongside team leads and fellow TPMs. You own execution – schedule, cross-disciplinary coordination, risk, and delivery. The engineers run the technical depth; you run the programme.

What You’ll Do 

· Own end-to-end execution of vehicle-level and subsystem product development programmes – from kick-off through hardware build, test campaigns, qualification, and delivery

· Build and maintain programme plans spanning propulsion, structures, avionics, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and regulatory dependencies; identify and resolve critical path risks early

· Run programme reviews and cross-functional coordination meetings; keep decisions documented and actions closed

· Background in aerospace, defence, or a similarly regulated hardware domain; familiarity with vehicle-level or system-level development and qualification cycles is essential

· Experience managing cross-disciplinary programmes spanning multiple engineering domains (structures, propulsion, avionics, or similar) is a strong advantage

title: Stress Engineer - Non-linear & Propellants
description:
The Destinus engineering team is seeking a Stress Engineer to support structural sizing and simulation with a focus on non-linear and thermomechanical analysis of solid rocket motor structures.

A core part of this role is the structural simulation of propellant grains, liner bonds, thermal protection systems (TPS), and propellant–liner–casing interfaces – combining FEA with material characterization and test correlation to build substantiated models of energetic material assemblies.

What You’ll Do 

· Conduct stress analysis using both classical hand-calculation methods and FEA – linear and non-linear, static and dynamic

· Simulate solid rocket motor structures: propellant grain stress and strain fields, bond integrity at propellant–liner and liner–casing interfaces, TPS thermomechanical response, and igniter/nozzle attachment loads

· Conduct non-linear simulations covering geometric non-linearity, material non-linearity (plasticity, hyperelasticity for propellant and elastomeric materials), and contact mechanics

· Perform thermomechanical analysis across metallic, composite, bonded, and polymeric structures under thermal cycling and operational loads

· Support experimental characterisation of propellant, liner, and bonded joint materials; feed test results (lap shear, peel, tensile, and DMA data) into material models and allowables

· Correlate FE predictions against strain gauge, load, and thermal test data; validate and update models accordingly

· Prepare stress reports, margin-of-safety calculations, and design justification documentation

Requirements 

What You’ll Need

· Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field

· 3–5 years of industry experience in stress analysis of aerospace or mechanical structures

· Proficiency with FEA packages: NASTRAN (Femap or equivalent), Abaqus, or Optistruct/HyperWorks for both linear and non-linear analysis

· Strong classical stress analysis skills: beam theory, buckling, fastener and joint analysis, margin-of-safety calculations

· Experience with non-linear material modelling – plasticity, hyperelasticity, or viscoelasticity; familiarity with propellant or elastomeric material constitutive models is a strong advantage

· Experience with thermomechanical or thermal-structural analysis

· Experience correlating FE predictions with experimental test data

· Background in solid rocket motor, propulsion, or energetic structures is a strong advantage

· Fluent in English; German or French is an advantage

We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are 

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

We are building industry-defining accounting and finance software. We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Accounting Solutions Consultant to join our team and help lead the successful onboarding of new customers onto Rillet.

This role is ideal for someone with a strong accounting foundation who is excited to work directly with customers and help finance teams modernize how they operate. You may come from Big 4 audit, accounting advisory, finance transformation, or an operational accounting role at a high-growth technology company. You do not need to have formally led ERP implementations before, but you do need to be systems-minded, highly organized, customer-oriented, and eager to learn quickly in a fast-paced startup environment.

We’re primarily looking for teammates who are based near our New York City or San Francisco offices, or open to relocating. For this role, we’re also open to remote candidates based anywhere in the United States. Our hybrid schedule brings office-based team members together in person on Tuesdays and Thursdays, plus one additional flexible day each week. Some roles may spend more time in the office depending on the needs of the team.

What You'll Do

- Lead key parts of customer onboarding and deployment, helping ensure a smooth and timely implementation experience

- Partner with internal teams across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to execute implementation plans and solve customer problems quickly

- Learn and analyze client accounting and finance workflows, then translate those needs into clear requirements and practical solutions

- Guide customers through onboarding, training, change management, and adoption

- Support data migration, reconciliations, systems setup, and integration coordination

- Track milestones, drive follow-through, and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned throughout the onboarding process

- Identify risks early, escalate issues quickly, and help keep customer launches on track

- Build trust with customers by being responsive, thoughtful, and solutions-oriented

- Maintain clear documentation and provide regular status updates to customers and internal stakeholders

Who We're Looking For

- 4-7 years of experience in accounting, audit, advisory, or related customer-facing roles

- Strong accounting foundation, with the ability to speak credibly about close, reconciliations, revenue recognition (ASC 606), and core finance workflows

- Excellent communication skills and the presence to work directly with customers and senior stakeholders

- Systems-minded and excited to learn implementation work, even if you have not formally held an implementation title before

- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams at once

- Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high attention to detail

- Experience working cross-functionally with technical and non-technical teams

- Experience in Big 4, SaaS or at a technology company is a plus

Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning! 

We are looking for... 

An enterprise seller who already knows the Office of the CFO. You've carried a number selling planning, EPM, FP&A or finance software. You know how a CFO buys, how a steering committee stalls, and how to get a multi-stakeholder deal signed.

At Abacum you'll own a named territory of enterprise and upper mid-market accounts across EMEA. Many of them run legacy planning tools or spreadsheets that can't keep up with the business. Your job is to show them a better foundation, and win.

As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will...

You know the category. Here's why this is the product you want in your bag.

1. A market ready to switch. Finance teams are stuck between rigid legacy planning tools that need a rebuild every time the business changes, and spreadsheets and AI tools no one can trust. 5. A product that keeps getting stronger. New AI skills ship every week. Abacum works where finance already works: Excel, Slack, Claude and ChatGPT, through MCP-native infrastructure. You'll have something new to show every quarter.

6. Funded to win enterprise. Abacum raised a $60M Series B to scale into larger customers. You'll join as we build the enterprise motion, with the room to shape it and grow with it.

- Remote in EMEA, with hubs in New York, Toronto and Barcelona

Benefits 

- Competitive compensation including equity package

- Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform)

Customer Obsession: We share the understanding that Abacum's sole purpose is to create value for customers and relentlessly deploy all creativity and energy to that end.

Audacious Ambition: We dream big and embrace discomfort. We assume risks, make on-time mistakes and learn how to methodically accomplish our goals.

Good People: We are self-reflective and praise diversity of thought. We don't justify the end with the means and know where to draw the line. We have fun every day.

Tough Love: We truly care for everyone in the team and embrace honest feedback and radical candor as ways to genuinely help each other.

title: Senior Backend Developer (Python, Java)
description:
Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we've been building that knowledge for over 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we're also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax advisors don't just get an answer, but an answer they're willing to attach their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it daily, generating over 100 million euros in ARR across Europe. We're looking for a Senior Backend Developer to help build that.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD 

Our Knowledge Team is the layer between the content and the AI. We pull in millions of documents from internal databases, public sources, and the web, standardize them, and make them usable for the AI agents that distill answers from them. The real challenge isn't storage but selection. Out of those millions of documents, exactly one paragraph needs to surface the moment a lawyer asks a question. Surface the wrong one, and the agent gives an answer that sounds plausible but is wrong. In our field, that's not a bug: it's a liability issue. What you build determines whether the answer holds up.

There's work to be done, and it's the kind of work you could talk about for a whole evening. The pipeline has been running for six years, built in Scala and Java, and parts of it deserve a new foundation. Reranking is the biggest need: determining which passage, out of a mountain of legal documents, actually answers the question being asked. Not just which one contains the matching words. That's the problem we’re solving. The team is strong on the scientific side, in retrieval, and in understanding what a model can and can't handle. What we're looking to add is engineering firepower: someone who can turn ideas into systems that deliver. Not to rebuild everything over six months just because it was once set up differently, but to see where the real gains are and start there.

- You build and improve the pipeline that turns content into knowledge our AI agents can use.

- You work on reranking quality, so the agent gets the right information, not just the most information.

- You help shape the approach to retrieval and knowledge extraction, bringing in what you've seen work elsewhere.

- You work in Python for everything new, and in Java where the existing codebase calls for it.

- You make technical decisions, even when no one is looking over your shoulder.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

You're an engineer who looks beyond the ticket. You want to understand why something is being built and what it delivers for the customer, and you're not afraid to have an opinion about it. You don't need a manager to make a technical call, and you speak up when you think something should be done differently.

- Experience with Python and Java. Everything newly built is developed in Python, closely aligned with the AI teams who also work in it. But a large part of our current codebase runs on Java, so you need to be comfortable working with that too.

- Experience with Elasticsearch. That's where it's determined which information the agent gets to see.

- Experience with Scala or Kotlin is a plus. The ingestion layer runs largely on Scala.

- You come from SaaS, a product-driven organization, or a scale-up, and you thrive on autonomy rather than oversight.

WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR 

At Lefebvre Sdu, you'll work in an organization that's in the middle of a transformation and takes the public market seriously. That's the direction, and we're making the journey together. You'll get the mandate, the space, and the colleagues to make it happen.

You'll join a team with a Product Owner, three frontend developers, a UX designer, and a Scrum Master who also works across multiple teams. You'll have room to shape your role and help determine how we work, with a clear shared goal: building the AI-first platform. You'll bring the backend experience the team needs to take real end-to-end ownership, and you'll report to the Lead Frontend Developer. You'll take part in the team's regular scrum rituals (dailies, refinements, retros, planning) and have one-on-ones with your manager. Through the team, you'll also be an important point of contact for application administrators and customer support who need technical assistance, so you should enjoy breaking down technical problems and communicating about them with less technical colleagues.

- A place where you have influence from day one: on the approach, the processes, and the direction.

- Colleagues who deliberately chose Lefebvre Sdu over big tech jobs because here, they're building something that doesn't exist yet.

- Base salary between €5,500 and €6,450 per month, based on a 36-hour week, since that's full-time for us. Plus a lot of extra allowances (see below).

- A bonus tied to company performance: a fixed year-end bonus of 4% and profit sharing of up to 6%.

- 23 vacation days and a personal choice budget of 12%, of which 8% is holiday pay and 4% is freely allocable. Want more vacation? Just buy it.

- A bonus of up to 10% of your salary, based on company performance and individual performance.

- A solid pension plan through PGB, including supplementary partner insurance.

- Collective insurance plans.

- A travel allowance of €0.25 per kilometer or a public transport reimbursement, plus an attractive bike plan. For employees with a commute of less than 10 km or more than 60 km, we have an adjusted arrangement.

- Two days a week in the office in The Hague, within walking distance of Voorburg station. The rest of the week, wherever you work best.

- Room to grow: in your craft, in your role, in the organization.

WANT TO KNOW MORE? 

We'd love to tell you all about the team and the role. Send us your CV and you'll hear from us within a few business days. Have a few questions first? Message or call Elize at 0641186590.

AI Solution Architecture

Enterprise Agent Architecture

Integration Architecture

AI Security and Governance

title: Director of Accounting & Controlling
description:
Imagine this. You are building the accounting and controlling backbone behind a fast-growing aerospace and defence company operating across multiple countries, manufacturing sites, and legal entities. As Director of Accounting & Controlling, you will own the integrity of our group financial reporting, set the standard for IFRS and local GAAP compliance, and make sure our numbers are accurate, controlled, scalable, and audit-ready.

Reporting directly to the CFO, you will be the group's senior technical accounting authority and a key finance leader across the organization. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage accounting from a distance. You will set the agenda, challenge existing processes, solve complex accounting issues, and drive execution across a distributed international finance organization.

At Destinus, we are revolutionizing the defense industry with cutting-edge Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our innovative technologies are designed to meet the unique demands of modern defense operations, delivering unparalleled speed, precision, and cost effectiveness. Destinus partners with government agencies and defense organizations worldwide to provide advanced solutions for mission-critical operations, enabling a new era of efficiency and technological superiority. Join us in shaping the future of defense with groundbreaking aerospace innovations.

What You'll Do 

- Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual group close across all consolidated entities, ensuring accurate, complete, and timely financial reporting
- Own the group close calendar and drive execution across Accounting, Controlling, FP&A, Tax, Treasury, and regional finance teams
- Act as the senior escalation point for complex accounting and close issues, driving them to resolution without compromising reporting quality or timelines
- Coordinate consolidation adjustments, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and other group-level accounting activities
- Own and continuously strengthen internal accounting controls, policies, and their consistent application across the group
- Drive improvements to our ERP and finance systems landscape, including Microsoft Dynamics environments, IFRS and local GAAP configurations, regional VAT setups, transfer pricing, intercompany eliminations, and consolidation processes
- Own group-wide cost accounting standards and methodologies across manufacturing entities, including standard and actual costing, absorption, WIP, and variance analysis
- Lead the Operations Finance function through the Operations Finance Lead and ensure disciplined capture and reporting of manufacturing costs including labor, overhead, scrap, absorption, and WIP
- Own the variance bridge process and ensure significant deviations are understood, explained, and assigned to the right accountable teams across Manufacturing, Program Management, Procurement, and Finance
- Connect Cost Accounting, Operations, Manufacturing, and Program Management so operational drivers such as volume, yield, labor mix, and capacity utilization are reflected in forecasts and budgets
- Partner closely with FP&A to ensure accounting actuals, forecasts, and budgets remain methodologically aligned as the business scales
- Own accounting judgments related to inventory, WIP, and program cost capitalization under IAS 2
- Govern the group chart of accounts and ensure it remains consistent, scalable, and aligned with consolidation and management reporting requirements
- Own balance sheet quality across the group, establishing clear standards for account ownership, reconciliations, substantiation, aging, suspense accounts, clearing accounts, and provisions
- Partner with FP&A and Treasury on working capital, provisions, capex accounting, and other balance sheet forecasting inputs
- Oversee AP and AR processes across the group, strengthening controls, segregation of duties, cash conversion, and sub-ledger reconciliation
- Drive DSO and DPO discipline and establish robust policies around credit control, payment terms, and dispute resolution
- Act as the primary management counterpart for external auditors across group and statutory audits
- Own audit timelines, PBC processes, technical accounting documentation, and the timely resolution of audit findings
- Ensure statutory financial statements are accurate and filed on time across jurisdictions in coordination with local teams and external advisors
- Support lender and investor diligence with accurate, audit-ready financial schedules and clear technical accounting narratives
- Standardize accounting processes and controls across entities and eliminate unnecessary manual workarounds as the organization grows
- Partner with IT and ERP teams to build scalable accounting, costing, consolidation, and reporting structures within systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365
- Own group accounting policies, procedures, and SOPs, creating a consistent framework for control, onboarding, and training
- Build and develop a high-performing accounting and controlling organization across multiple European jurisdictions, setting clear expectations and creating accountability across direct and indirect teams
- Mentor Controllers and Accounting Managers across the group and act as the technical escalation point when complex accounting decisions need to be made
Requirements 

What You'll Need 

- 10+ years of progressive Accounting, Controlling, or Finance experience, including substantial responsibility within a multi-entity, multi-currency European environment
- Public company experience is required
- Deep technical knowledge of IFRS and strong familiarity with local GAAP requirements across European jurisdictions
- Demonstrated experience owning group accounting policies and making complex technical accounting judgments
- Proven experience leading group close and consolidation processes at significant scale, ideally within environments exceeding EUR 1 billion in revenue
- Strong manufacturing cost accounting experience, including standard and actual costing, variance analysis, absorption, inventory, and WIP
- Experience working closely with Manufacturing and Operations teams, with the ability to connect operational performance with financial outcomes
- Strong ERP experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle, or an equivalent large-scale platform, including exposure to chart-of-accounts design, costing structures, consolidation, and finance transformation
- Experience leading geographically distributed finance teams and developing senior accounting and controlling professionals
- Excellent English communication skills, with additional European languages considered an advantage
- Experience within aerospace, defence, industrial manufacturing, or another regulated and program-driven environment is strongly preferred
- Experience with statutory reporting requirements across multiple European jurisdictions is a strong advantage
- Familiarity with program-based revenue recognition, government or institutional customers, and complex manufacturing environments is an advantage.

Who You Are 

You combine technical accounting depth with the drive to get things done. You care about clean numbers, strong controls, and clear ownership, but you also understand that Finance needs to move at the speed of the business.

You are comfortable being the person people turn to when the accounting answer is not obvious. You challenge assumptions, translate complex IFRS topics into practical decisions, and know when to go deep and when to move quickly.

You think beyond the next close. You build processes, systems, and teams that can support a company as it grows across countries, manufacturing sites, and increasingly complex operations. You work naturally across Accounting, FP&A, Treasury, Tax, Manufacturing, Operations, and leadership, and you are persistent about getting decisions and open issues to closure.

Most importantly, you build capability around you. You develop strong teams, create accountability, and make sure critical accounting knowledge is embedded across the organization rather than concentrated in one person.

title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
Grip is changing how global brands produce content - from manual, tool-driven workflows to intelligent systems that generate high-quality visual output at scale. 

As a Senior AI Engineer, you build the intelligence behind that shift: LLM agents that understand what a brand looks like, retrieval systems that ground every generation in real brand knowledge, and automated pipelines that turn messy client material into structure machines can work with. 

The hard problem in generative AI is no longer generation. It's control, consistency, and trust — making unpredictable models behave reliably for brands that care deeply about how they show up in the world. That's the problem you'll own. 

What You'll Work On 

- LLM agents - designing focused, reliable agents that translate brand intent into precise creative direction 

- Prompt engineering & orchestration - crafting, testing, and versioning the prompts that steer agents and generation, and building the system that assembles them - prompting as an engineering discipline, not trial and error 

- Retrieval & RAG - grounding generation in each brand's rules, assets, and visual language, with strict isolation between clients 

- Evaluation & experimentation - systematic measurement (RAGAS or similar), A/B testing, and regression gates, so quality is proven rather than assumed 

- Data extraction & OCR - pipelines that pull structure out of documents, decks, scans, and imagery; OCR and vision models for reading, understanding, and tagging whatever a client hands us 

- Automation - end-to-end pipelines that run without babysitting: classify, extract, propose, verify - humans review outcomes instead of doing the work by hand 

- Model training - fine-tuning LLMs and neural networks where prompting hits its ceiling, running models locally or hosted depending on what the job needs 

- Client-facing impact - your pipelines run against real client data and real production volume, and the results are visible in everything that ships 

Who You Are 

You build systems that make AI predictable, controllable, and production-ready — especially in visual domains. 

You Have: 

- Strong experience with LLM-based systems in production (agents, RAG, orchestration) 

- Hands-on work with evaluation frameworks and structured experimentation — quality you can prove, not claim 

- Solid programming skills across TypeScript and Python, with experience shipping working systems 

- Experience training or fine-tuning models and managing their lifecycle 

- Exposure to generative image pipelines and what it takes to make their output usable (not theoretical interest — actual contact) 

You Think: 

- In systems, not prompts — how components interact, fail, and scale 

- In constraints — how to guide models toward predictable outputs 

- In data — extraction, classification, and structure as the foundation everything else stands on 

- Pragmatically — you ship working solutions and refine based on results 

Your Skills Are: 

- Translating abstract creative direction into structured AI workflows 

- Turning messy, unstructured material into clean, reliable data pipelines 

- Debugging LLM and retrieval behavior across multiple layers of a pipeline 

- Communicating across engineering and creative teams 

Why Join Grip? 

The Platform Position. 
Grip is infrastructure for enterprise creative production—powering global brands to generate content at scale with control and consistency. 

The Market Timing. 
AI-generated content is moving from experimentation to production. The challenge is no longer generation—it’s control, reliability, and scale. 

The Technical Moat. 
You’ll work with ComfyUI-based workflows, multi-tenant architecture, and a stack spanning TypeScript, Python, Elixir, and C#—built for production, not demos. 

The Work. 
You will define how AI is actually used in real-world creative systems—turning unpredictable models into dependable pipelines.

description:
INDG is expanding the way high-volume visual content is produced: from CGI and 3D pipelines into AI-assisted image generation, editing, and content orchestration. This role exists to help turn generative AI from an experimental layer into a reliable production capability. 

As a Generative-AI Artist (freelance) , you will build and run image generation workflows that support real client production: fashion, sportswear, product imagery, talent visuals, campaign adaptations, and asset variation at scale. You will work inside the tension that defines this role: fast-moving AI models, production deadlines, visual realism, brand consistency, and systems that other people can actually use. 

INDG has spent 20+ years building visual production systems for global brands. Grip extends that heritage into AI-orchestrated content production. Your work will help teams generate, edit, refine, and scale imagery while keeping outputs sharp enough for enterprise brand use. 

What You Will Do 

Build and Maintain Generative Image Workflows 

Set up, configure, and troubleshoot custom ComfyUI workflows for image generation, image editing, inpainting, outpainting, upscaling, relighting, variation generation, and controlled composition. 

You will connect models, nodes, prompts, masks, ControlNet inputs, LoRAs, reference images, and post-processing steps into repeatable workflows. The goal is not a one-off good image. The goal is a workflow that can produce consistent, usable outputs across many assets. 

Apply AI to Production Content Problems 

Use generative AI techniques against real production needs: adjusting apparel/footwear/accessories/equipment imagery, refining fashion/sportswear product shots, extending scenes, improving model consistency, generating controlled variations, or supporting creative teams with rapid image exploration. 

You should understand that production images are judged on details: skin texture, garment fit, fabric behavior, seams, logos, lighting direction, pose plausibility, background continuity, and whether the image still feels brand-correct after generation. 

Adapt Quickly as Models and Tools Change 

Work confidently across diffusion-based models, LoRAs, ControlNet, IP-Adapter-style workflows, segmentation tools, inpainting models, outpainting methods, face and identity consistency techniques, and emerging image-generation systems. 

You will test new models, identify where they improve or break the pipeline, and help the team decide when a tool is production-ready. You do not need every new release to be perfect. You need to know how to evaluate it, isolate failure modes, and translate it into a usable workflow. 

Support a Pipeline Used by Artists and Production Teams 

Document workflows clearly enough for artists, producers, and technical teams to reuse them. Package settings, prompts, node graphs, model dependencies, and output criteria in a way that reduces guesswork. 

You will work with CGI artists, creative technologists, production leads, and platform teams to connect creative intent with operational execution. When something fails, you trace the system: model choice, conditioning input, prompt structure, mask quality, render reference, node configuration, or post-process step. 

Who You Are 

You live at the intersection of image-making and systems-building. You care about the final image, but you also care about the workflow that created it. 

You Have 

Hands-on experience building and maintaining ComfyUI workflows, or comparable node-based generative AI systems. 

A strong working knowledge of current image-generation methods: diffusion models, LoRAs, ControlNet, inpainting, outpainting, image-to-image workflows, upscaling, masking, reference-based generation, and controlled variation. 

Experience producing or refining commercial-quality imagery. Fashion, sportswear, product, talent, ecommerce, campaign adaptation, or CGI production experience is a strong plus. 

You Think 

Systems-first. A good prompt is useful; a repeatable workflow is better. 

Automation-first. Manual fixes are acceptable only when they teach the pipeline what to solve next. 

Visually. You can tell when an image fails because of lighting, anatomy, garment behavior, material response, identity drift, composition, or post-processing artifacts. 

Your Skills Are 

ComfyUI workflow construction, debugging, model loading, node graph organization, and dependency management. 

Practical prompt engineering for controlled output, not prompt decoration. 

Image evaluation for realism, consistency, brand fit, and production usability. 

Comfort with fast tool changes, incomplete documentation, broken nodes, model conflicts, and solving problems directly. 

Why Join INDG 

INDG has spent more than two decades building CGI, 3D, and visual production systems for global brands. Grip now orchestrates AI workflows and production-grade outputs across that same visual heritage. 

This freelance role is for someone who wants to work where generative AI meets real production pressure: brand consistency, scale, quality control, and images that need to hold up beyond a demo.

Jouw rol 

Als Business Unit Director OtO ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor een internationaal portfolio van operationele assets én voor de organisatie die dit portfolio naar de volgende fase van professionalisering en schaalbare groei brengt. Wie ben jij? 

Je bent een ervaren leider die gewend is om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen voor complexe, kapitaalintensieve assets en internationale teams. Je combineert strategisch overzicht met voldoende operationele scherpte om te weten waar performance in de praktijk wordt gemaakt. HoSt Group is een internationale technologieleider op het gebied van duurzame energieoplossingen. title: Junior Talent Acquisition Partner (m/w/d)
description:
Davon träumen wir: Mehr als Recruiting. Die richtigen Menschen für die richtigen Aufgaben. 

VielfaltMenü befindet sich in einer Phase der Weiterentwicklung. Wir schärfen unsere Organisation, professionalisieren unsere Prozesse und richten uns noch konsequenter auf unsere Kund:innen, unsere Mitarbeiter:innen und nachhaltiges Wachstum aus. 
Dazu gehört auch ein neues Verständnis von Recruiting. 
Wir wollen Stellen nicht einfach besetzen. Wir wollen verstehen, welche Kompetenzen wir wirklich benötigen, wie wir sie erkennen und welche Menschen zu unserer Organisation und unseren Zielen passen. 

Dafür suchen wir dich als Junior Talent Acquisition Partner:in 

Du musst nicht bereits zehn Jahre Recruiting-Erfahrung mitbringen. 
Entscheidend sind für uns analytisches Denken, Neugier, ein ausgeprägter Qualitätsanspruch und die Fähigkeit, Menschen und Kompetenzen gut einzuschätzen. 

Deine Aufgaben 
Du begleitest Recruitingprozesse von der ersten Anforderungsanalyse bis zum unterschriebenen Arbeitsvertrag und entwickelst gemeinsam mit People & Culture unsere Recruitingstandards weiter. 
Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unseren Führungskräften und der Geschäftsführung zusammen. 
Talent Acquisition & Beratung 
Du führst strukturierte Briefings mit Führungskräften und übersetzt Anforderungen in klare Kompetenz- und Kandidatenprofile. 
Du berätst Führungskräfte bei der Auswahl geeigneter Kandidat:innen und sprichst auch dann eine klare Empfehlung aus, wenn die einfachste Lösung nicht die beste ist. 
Interviews führst du eigenständig – vom operativen Recruiting bis hin zu Gesprächen auf Managementebene. 
Kompetenzorientierte Auswahl 
Wir wollen Auswahlentscheidungen stärker auf Kompetenzen und nachvollziehbare Kriterien stützen. 
Du entwickelst strukturierte Interviewleitfäden, Bewertungsmatrizen und Auswahlstandards und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Entscheidungen vergleichbarer und belastbarer werden. 
Bei diagnostischen Auswahlverfahren und Assessments begleitest du Konzeption, Durchführung und Auswertung. 
Dein Anspruch dabei: weniger Bauchgefühl, mehr Qualität in der Entscheidung . 
Candidate Experience & Kreativität 
Professionelle Prozesse dürfen trotzdem persönlich sein. 
Du entwickelst Ideen, wie wir Kandidat:innen besser erreichen und ihnen vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Einstellung eine überzeugende Candidate Experience bieten. 
Dabei probierst du neue Recruitingwege aus, hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse und entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns moderne Recruitingformate. 
Vertragsmanagement & Prozesse 
Du steuerst den Recruitingprozess zuverlässig bis zum Vertragsabschluss. 
Du bereitest Vertragsangebote vor, koordinierst Abstimmungen und sorgst dafür, dass Vereinbarungen vollständig, korrekt und termingerecht umgesetzt werden. 
Arbeitsrechtliche und datenschutzrechtliche Fragestellungen erkennst du und kannst sie gemeinsam mit People & Culture bzw. unserer juristischen Expertise einordnen. 
Du arbeitest strukturiert, standardisiert und detailgenau – ohne dabei unnötige Bürokratie aufzubauen. 

Was du mitbringst 
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium, beispielsweise in Wirtschaftspsychologie, Psychologie, Personalmanagement, Wirtschafts- oder Rechtswissenschaften, oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation. 
Erste praktische Erfahrung im Recruiting, Talent Acquisition, HR oder in der Personalauswahl ist hilfreich – beispielsweise durch Werkstudententätigkeiten, Praktika oder deine erste berufliche Station. 
Auch wenn du am Anfang deiner Karriere stehst, freuen wir uns ausdrücklich auf deine Bewerbung. 
Wichtiger als die Anzahl deiner Berufsjahre ist für uns, wie du denkst und arbeitest. 
Du hast Interesse an eignungsdiagnostischen und kompetenzorientierten Auswahlverfahren. 
Du kannst Gespräche strukturieren, genau zuhören, kritisch nachfragen und deine Einschätzung anschließend nachvollziehbar begründen. 
Du hast ein gutes Verständnis für wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge und keine Scheu davor, mit Führungskräften und Geschäftsführung auf Augenhöhe zu diskutieren. 
Juristische Fragestellungen – insbesondere rund um Arbeitsverträge und Arbeitsrecht – schrecken dich nicht ab. Idealerweise bringst du bereits entsprechende Grundkenntnisse mit. 
Du arbeitest sehr sorgfältig und hast gleichzeitig Freude daran, Dinge neu zu denken. 

Was uns bei dir besonders wichtig ist 
Kreativität . 
Du akzeptierst nicht automatisch, dass Recruiting so funktionieren muss, wie es schon immer funktioniert hat. 
Struktur. 
Du glaubst an Standards, klare Prozesse und nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen. 
Detailorientierung. 
Ein falsches Datum im Arbeitsvertrag ist für dich keine Kleinigkeit. 
Urteilsvermögen. 
Du möchtest verstehen, welche Kompetenzen jemand wirklich mitbringt – und nicht nur, wie gut sich jemand präsentieren kann. 
Mut zur Empfehlung. 
Von dir erwarten wir nicht nur Organisation. Wir wollen deine Einschätzung hören. 
Neugier. 
Du möchtest verstehen, wie unser Geschäft funktioniert und was unsere Führungskräfte und Teams erfolgreich macht. 

Was dich bei VielfaltMenü erwartet 
VielfaltMenü steht für „Mehr als gutes Essen.“ 
Wir versorgen täglich Menschen in Bildungseinrichtungen und entwickeln uns als Unternehmen kontinuierlich weiter. People & Culture soll dabei nicht nur verwalten, sondern die Entwicklung des Unternehmens aktiv unterstützen. Du bekommst deshalb die Möglichkeit, unser Recruiting nicht nur auszuführen, sondern mitzugestalten . Du arbeitest eng mit Führungskräften, dem People & Culture-Team sowie der Geschäftsführung zusammen und erhältst früh Verantwortung für eigene Recruitingprozesse. Gleichzeitig geben wir dir Raum, dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln. 
In deiner Rolle genießt du echten Gestaltungsspielraum : Du baust moderne Qualitäts- sowie Prozessstrukturen aktiv mit auf und prägst die Standards eines führenden Unternehmens für Kita- und Schulverpflegung in Deutschland. Dabei profitierst du von kurzen Entscheidungswegen und einer Geschäftsführung, die Qualität strategisch fördert. 
Neben einem unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag in einem zukunftssicheren Markt erwarten dich eine attraktive, transparente Vergütung sowie klare Entwicklungsperspektiven durch strukturierte Einarbeitung und individuelle Weiterbildungen. Wir unterstützen deine Work-Life-Balance durch 30 Urlaubstage , geregelte Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten. Zudem erhältst du moderne Arbeitsmittel inklusive Diensthandy. Eine gute ÖPNV-Anbindung und ein engagiertes, kollegiales Team runden unser Angebot ab. 

Klingt nach dir? 
Dann interessiert uns nicht nur dein Lebenslauf. 
Wir möchten wissen, wie du über Menschen, Kompetenzen und gute Personalauswahl denkst. 
Bewirb dich bei uns und gestalte gemeinsam mit uns, wie Recruiting bei VielfaltMenü künftig funktioniert. 

VielfaltMenü – Mehr als gutes Essen.

We're looking for an enthusiastic frontend engineer with the skills and ability to turn great ideas into reality. Your input will help us grow and maintain our React front-end.

Join a team that encourages you to explore, learn, and go beyond, while seeing your work lead to actionable results. Put your creative problem-solving and development skills into action and make a positive impact on science and society. This is a full-time position based in Germany.

The team 

You will be an integral part of the product team dedicated to enhancing ResearchGate's publisher-facing product. This role involves designing, constructing, and refining the platform to further our mission of facilitating global scientific connections and ensuring open access to research. At present, our team is working on making ResearchGate a great platform for publishers to connect with existing and future authors.

Your immediate colleagues will consist of JavaScript and PHP engineers, an Engineering Manager, a Product Manager, a UX Designer, and a UX Writer. Our team places great value on our collaborative and communicative work culture and we eagerly anticipate integrating a new Engineer into this environment.

-

- 
Maintain and improve existing features and related infrastructure.

- 
Collaborate with Product Managers, Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver compelling publisher-facing products.

Requirements 

- 
5+ years frontend web development experience in TypeScript (React), CSS

- 
Demonstrated ability to create code that is easily comprehensible, maintainable, and testable.

- 
Eagerness to acquire new skills, delve into different technologies and programming languages, and a willingness to acknowledge areas where expertise may be lacking.

- 
Approach problem-solving thoughtfully, embracing curiosity and maintaining an open-minded perspective.

- 
You are comfortable incorporating AI-assisted development tools into your daily workflow and exercise strong engineering judgment when evaluating and refining their output.

- 
Knowledge of GraphQL.

- 
It would be a plus if you already had knowledge of relational and document-based databases (we use MongoDB and Postgres).

What we're looking for 

- 
You take responsibility over your own solutions and continuously improve them.

- 
You engage in proactive and efficient communication within our distributed work environment.

- 
You focus on building a great product.

- 
You excel at designing and creating coherent, user-centric interfaces that display complex information.

The interview process

- 
We start with a short call with HR or an Engineering Manager to align on the details of the job inquiry.

Last but not least, you will meet with our CEO, Ijad, and our VP of Finance & People team, Jess.
